controls.evidence: The rule object from `oci network nsg rules list --nsg-id <ocid> --all` showing id (the opaque rule identifier, not an OCID), direction=INGRESS, source-type, source, protocol, is-stateless and the complete tcp-options object including a null destination-port-range where present, together with the NSG OCID, its vcn-id and compartment-id, and the region.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when, across all subscribed regions, no NSG rule has direction=INGRESS AND source-type=CIDR_BLOCK AND source="0.0.0.0/0" AND protocol in {"6","all"} AND (tcp-options is absent OR tcp-options.destination-port-range is null OR destination-port-range.min <= 22 <= destination-port-range.max by numeric comparison). The verdict is only valid if `nsg rules list` was actually called with --all for every enumerated NSG; an NSG whose rules were never fetched is inconclusive, not a pass.
controls.remediation: Remove or narrow the rule: `oci network nsg rules remove --nsg-id <ocid> --security-rule-ids '["<rule_id>"]'` using the id string returned by `nsg rules list`, or `oci network nsg rules update --nsg-id <ocid> --security-rules file://rules.json` with source set to an administrative CIDR and an explicit destination-port-range, or better with source-type NETWORK_SECURITY_GROUP referencing the bastion NSG.
controls.caveat: The dominant false pass is checking the NSG object alone — `oci network nsg get` and Resource Search (including `return allAdditionalFields`) never carry the rule bodies, so an assessor who never calls `nsg rules list` sees zero findings. The second is a tcp-options object with a null destination-port-range, which opens all ports while looking like a scoped rule. Also: source-type may be NETWORK_SECURITY_GROUP or SERVICE_CIDR_BLOCK, neither of which is internet exposure and both of which must be excluded before flagging; the security-rule id is an opaque short string, not an OCID, so tooling that validates it as an OCID before calling `rules remove` will refuse to remediate; rules are paginated, so omitting --all truncates the list and yields a false pass on large NSGs; an NSG with no attached VNICs still fails the control; and NSGs are regional and per-VCN, so the region loop is mandatory.

controls.title: No security group exposes remote desktop access to the whole internet
controls.objective: An NSG ingress rule admitting the internet to RDP places Windows hosts one credential guess away from compromise regardless of subnet-level security lists, because NSG and security list rules are unioned, not intersected.
controls.procedure: Identical traversal to 2.3 with the port changed. Resolve the region set with `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy_ocid>` and drive `--region` from its region-name values. Per region: enumerate NSGs via `oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query NetworkSecurityGroup resources" --region <region> --all`, with the fallback `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all` plus `oci network nsg list --compartment-id <c> --all --region <region>`. Then `oci network nsg rules list --nsg-id <ocid> --all --region <region>`. Flag direction INGRESS, source-type CIDR_BLOCK, source 0.0.0.0/0, protocol "6" or "all", and tcp-options absent, or tcp-options present with destination-port-range null, or a destination-port-range whose min <= 3389 <= max.
api: oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query NetworkSecurityGroup resources" --region <region> --all
oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all  # --include-root takes no value
oci network nsg rules remove --nsg-id <nsg_ocid> --security-rule-ids '["<rule_id>"]' --region <region>  # rule ids are opaque strings, not OCIDs
oci network nsg rules update --nsg-id <nsg_ocid> --security-rules file://rules.json --region <region>
controls.evidence: The INGRESS rule entry returned by `oci network nsg rules list --all` (rule id, source-type, source, protocol, is-stateless, and the whole tcp-options object with destination-port-range or its explicit null) plus the owning NSG OCID, its vcn-id, compartment-id and region, and the list of subscribed regions actually swept.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when no NSG rule in any subscribed region has direction=INGRESS AND source-type=CIDR_BLOCK AND source="0.0.0.0/0" AND protocol in {"6","all"} AND (tcp-options is absent OR tcp-options.destination-port-range is null OR destination-port-range.min <= 3389 <= destination-port-range.max by numeric comparison). A run whose region set was not derived from `oci iam region-subscription list` is inconclusive rather than PASS.
controls.remediation: Delete the rule with `oci network nsg rules remove --nsg-id <ocid> --security-rule-ids '["<rule_id>"]'` or re-scope it via `oci network nsg rules update --nsg-id <ocid> --security-rules file://rules.json` to the jump-host NSG or corporate CIDRs with an explicit destination-port-range, and expose administrative access through OCI Bastion or a site-to-site VPN instead.
controls.caveat: Same rule-body trap as 2.3 (NSG metadata carries no rules) plus three more. Range trap: catch-all ranges like 1-65535 or 3000-4000 include 3389 without the literal string, so containment must be numeric, and a tcp-options object whose destination-port-range is null is wider than any range and must fail. Region trap: the verdict quantifies over subscribed regions, so `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy_ocid>` must be the first call and the source of every `--region` value — an implementer who omits it runs against the CLI profile's default region only and reports a single-region tenancy as clean. Pagination trap: omitting --all truncates the rule list and yields a false pass on large NSGs. Finally, this control and 2.2 are independent: a clean NSG result does not clear the subnet security lists, and both must pass before administrative exposure is genuinely closed. A udp-options rule spanning 3389 from 0.0.0.0/0 is real RDP exposure and should be reported as an accompanying observation.

controls.title: A VCN's auto-created list is never the thing that lets traffic in
controls.objective: Each VCN is born with a default security list that OCI attaches to any subnet created without an explicit list, and its shipped rules admit SSH from anywhere and permit all egress to anywhere; leaving it as-is silently grants internet ingress to future subnets and unrestricted outbound from them. Only intra-VCN ICMP path-MTU traffic should survive on the ingress side, and egress should not remain wide open.
controls.procedure: Per subscribed region (`oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy_ocid>`) list VCNs with `oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query Vcn resources" --region <region> --all` (fallback: `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all` then `oci network vcn list --compartment-id <c> --all --region <region>`). For each VCN run `oci network vcn get --vcn-id <ocid>` and capture default-security-list-id together with the VCN's complete prefix set: cidr-blocks (IPv4), ipv6-cidr-blocks and ipv6-private-cidr-blocks (IPv6). Fetch the list with `oci network security-list get --security-list-id <default_id>` and evaluate BOTH arrays. Ingress: every entry must be protocol "1" (ICMP) with a source contained in one of the IPv4 prefixes, or protocol "58" (ICMPv6) with a source contained in one of the IPv6 prefixes — match each protocol against the address family it belongs to, never IPv6 sources against cidr-blocks. Any TCP/UDP entry, or any source outside the VCN's own prefixes, fails. Egress: every entry must be destination-type CIDR_BLOCK with a destination contained in the VCN's own IPv4 or IPv6 prefixes, or destination-type SERVICE_CIDR_BLOCK naming a service-gateway destination the organisation has explicitly approved; a 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 egress rule fails.
api: oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query Vcn resources" --region <region> --all

oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all  # fallback walk; --include-root takes no value
oci network security-list update --security-list-id <default_security_list_ocid> --ingress-security-rules file://icmp_only.json --egress-security-rules file://egress.json --force
controls.evidence: From `oci network vcn get`: default-security-list-id plus the full prefix set (cidr-blocks, ipv6-cidr-blocks, ipv6-private-cidr-blocks). From `oci network security-list get` for exactly that OCID: the complete ingress-security-rules AND egress-security-rules arrays. For every rule record which prefix list its source or destination matched (IPv4 cidr-blocks, ipv6-cidr-blocks, ipv6-private-cidr-blocks, or none), so an IPv6 rule is never recorded as unmatched merely because it was compared against the IPv4 list.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when, for every VCN in every subscribed region, the security list at default-security-list-id satisfies both of: (a) ingress-security-rules is empty or contains only rules with protocol "1" whose source CIDR is contained in the union of that VCN's cidr-blocks, or protocol "58" whose source CIDR is contained in the union of that VCN's ipv6-cidr-blocks and ipv6-private-cidr-blocks; AND (b) egress-security-rules is empty or contains only rules whose destination-type is CIDR_BLOCK with a destination contained in that VCN's own IPv4/IPv6 prefixes, or destination-type SERVICE_CIDR_BLOCK for an explicitly approved service destination. Any TCP/UDP ingress entry, any 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 source or destination, or an ICMPv6 rule sourced outside the VCN's IPv6 prefixes is a FAIL.
controls.remediation: Strip the shipped rules on both sides in one call, since an update that supplies only one array leaves the other exactly as shipped: `oci network security-list update --security-list-id <default_id> --ingress-security-rules '[{"protocol":"1","source":"<vcn_ipv4_cidr>","sourceType":"CIDR_BLOCK","icmpOptions":{"type":3,"code":4}}]' --egress-security-rules '[]' --force` (add a protocol "58" entry sourced from the VCN's IPv6 prefix on dual-stack VCNs), and attach purpose-built security lists or NSGs to each subnet so nothing depends on the default list.
controls.caveat: Do not identify the default list by display name — "Default Security List for <vcn>" is fully editable, and a renamed default or a custom list coincidentally named that way breaks name-based matching in both directions; the only authoritative pointer is vcn.default-security-list-id. Second trap: auditing only lists currently attached to subnets skips the common case of an untouched default list sitting unused, which is precisely the risk this control addresses. Third: the shipped ICMP 3/4 rule is sourced 0.0.0.0/0 by default and must be re-sourced to the VCN CIDR — it looks harmless and is routinely left in place. Fourth, and newly load-bearing: the VCN's IPv6 prefixes never appear in cidr-blocks, so validating an ICMPv6 source against cidr-blocks alone scores a correctly-scoped dual-stack rule as FAIL and, worse, invites an implementer to "fix" it by skipping protocol 58 entirely — build the allowed-source set as the union of cidr-blocks, ipv6-cidr-blocks and ipv6-private-cidr-blocks and match per address family. Fifth: the default list also ships an all-protocols egress rule to 0.0.0.0/0, so checking ingress only lets a completely untouched default list score PASS; both arrays are in scope here, and a single-array `security-list update` silently preserves the other.

controls.title: Confine Integration Cloud instances to a private endpoint or a narrow source allowlist
controls.objective: An OIC instance published with an unrestricted public endpoint exposes its design-time console and REST integration endpoints to the entire internet, so reachability must be cut to a private endpoint or an explicit list of approved source networks.
controls.procedure: Walk compartments with `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all` (`--include-root` is a valueless flag; use ANY rather than ACCESSIBLE so compartments visible only indirectly are not dropped) and, per subscribed region from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy_ocid>`, run `oci integration integration-instance list --compartment-id <c> --all --region <region>`. For each instance call `oci integration integration-instance get --integration-instance-id <ocid>` and read network-endpoint-details. Do not assume the discriminator can be PRIVATE_ENDPOINT: confirm the enum against the live schema first — `oci integration integration-instance get --integration-instance-id <ocid> --query 'data."network-endpoint-details"'` against a known-restricted instance, or the Integration API specification — because PUBLIC appears to be the only value this discriminator takes, OIC private connectivity being expressed through separate private-endpoint constructs rather than through this enum. Within a PUBLIC endpoint read allowlisted-http-ips, allowlisted-http-vcns (each entry carrying id and allowlisted-ip-cidrs, which must be inspected individually) and is-integration-vcn-allowlisted. A null network-endpoint-details is fully open, not unconfigured.
api: oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all

oci integration integration-instance get --integration-instance-id <integration_instance_ocid> --query 'data."network-endpoint-details"'  # confirm the live discriminator values before pinning the verdict
oci search resource-type list --region <region>  # confirm IntegrationInstance is an indexed type before relying on Search
oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query IntegrationInstance resources" --region <region> --all
controls.evidence: The complete network-endpoint-details block of `oci integration integration-instance get` — network-endpoint-type, allowlisted-http-ips, allowlisted-http-vcns (recording each entry's id AND its nested allowlisted-ip-cidrs individually) and is-integration-vcn-allowlisted (the documented attribute name; a collector keyed on is-integration-vcn-only-allowlist reads null and records "not configured" for an instance that is in fact restricted to the integration VCN) — recorded against the instance OCID, lifecycle-state, compartment-id and region, with the explicit null state of network-endpoint-details captured as its own evidence value.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when every integration instance whose lifecycle-state is not DELETED or DELETING has a non-null network-endpoint-details whose network-endpoint-type equals the schema-confirmed public value (PUBLIC) AND at least one of allowlisted-http-ips non-empty, allowlisted-http-vcns non-empty, or is-integration-vcn-allowlisted == true, AND, after normalising every allowlist entry — top-level allowlisted-http-ips plus each VCN entry's nested allowlisted-ip-cidrs — to a CIDR, no single entry has prefix length 0 and the interval-merged union of all entries does not cover the entire 32-bit IPv4 address space (nor the entire IPv6 space if IPv6 entries are present). A null or absent network-endpoint-details is a FAIL. An instance exempt because inbound access is genuinely private must be evidenced from its private-endpoint configuration, never from an unverified PRIVATE_ENDPOINT enum value. The residual judgement — whether the surviving, strictly narrower ranges are organisationally approved — is the Manual overlay and is stated as such.
controls.remediation: Apply an allowlist with `oci integration integration-instance change-network-endpoint --integration-instance-id <ocid> --network-endpoint-details file://endpoint.json` specifying allowlistedHttpIps for the approved CIDRs, allowlistedHttpVcns (each with its own narrow allowlistedIpCidrs) for internal callers, and isIntegrationVcnAllowlisted where the integration VCN is the intended caller. Where inbound access should not traverse the internet at all, place the instance behind the service's private-endpoint configuration rather than relying on an allowlist.
controls.caveat: Marked Manual because the API can prove an allowlist exists but not that it is meaningful — only a human who knows which networks are approved can adjudicate the surviving ranges. Four mechanical traps must not be left to that judgement, though. (1) a complementary pair of /1 halves (the low half plus the high half), or a set of /8s, is exactly equivalent to a /0 while matching no single 0.0.0.0/0 entry; the test must be prefix-length-0 detection plus an interval-merge union check over the address space, not string equality. (2) The attribute is is-integration-vcn-allowlisted, not is-integration-vcn-only-allowlist; the wrong key reads null and mislabels a restricted instance as unconfigured. (3) A null network-endpoint-details reads like "nothing configured" but means unrestricted public access, so it is a FAIL. (4) The PRIVATE_ENDPOINT branch may be dead code — PUBLIC appears to be the only documented value of this discriminator — so an assessor who sees no PRIVATE_ENDPOINT instances may believe the check is exercised when only one branch has ever run; confirm the enum against the live schema and, if it is PUBLIC-only, drop the branch rather than leaving it as an untested exemption. Also: a listed VCN whose nested allowlisted-ip-cidrs is wide is not a restriction; and OIC instances are regional and compartment-scoped, so a root-compartment-only or home-region-only sweep misses whole estates. Confirm the Search resource type name with `oci search resource-type list` before relying on it.

controls.title: Confine Analytics Cloud instances to a VCN endpoint or an explicit IP allowlist
controls.objective: An OAC instance with an open public endpoint puts a full BI console and its data connections on the internet; access should terminate on a private VCN endpoint or be limited to enumerated source IPs and VCNs.
controls.procedure: Enumerate compartments with `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all` (`--include-root` is valueless; ANY rather than ACCESSIBLE so no compartment is silently dropped) and loop subscribed regions from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy_ocid>` with `oci analytics analytics-instance list --compartment-id <c> --all --region <region>`. For each, run `oci analytics analytics-instance get --analytics-instance-id <ocid>` and read network-endpoint-details: network-endpoint-type PRIVATE carries vcn-id, subnet-id and network-security-group-ids; PUBLIC carries whitelisted-ips and whitelisted-vcns, each VCN entry carrying its own id and nested whitelisted-ips which must be inspected individually. Treat a null or absent network-endpoint-details as an unrestricted public endpoint, not as unconfigured. Where the endpoint is PRIVATE, follow network-security-group-ids into `oci network nsg rules list --nsg-id <ocid> --all` so a private endpoint fronted by an internet-open NSG is not scored as restricted.
api: oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all
oci search resource-type list --region <region>  # confirm AnalyticsInstance is an indexed type before relying on Search
oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query AnalyticsInstance resources" --region <region> --all
oci network nsg rules list --nsg-id <nsg_ocid> --all --region <region>  # for PRIVATE endpoints, prove the fronting NSGs are not internet-open
controls.evidence: The complete network-endpoint-details object from `oci analytics analytics-instance get` — network-endpoint-type, and either vcn-id/subnet-id/network-security-group-ids or the whitelisted-ips array and the whitelisted-vcns array with each entry's id AND its nested whitelisted-ips — captured with the instance OCID, lifecycle-state, compartment-id and region, recording an absent or null network-endpoint-details as its own explicit evidence value. For PRIVATE instances, also the ingress rule set of each referenced NSG.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when every analytics instance whose lifecycle-state is not DELETED or DELETING has a non-null network-endpoint-details and either (a) network-endpoint-type=PRIVATE with a non-null subnet-id, and no NSG in network-security-group-ids carries an INGRESS rule from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0; or (b) network-endpoint-type=PUBLIC with whitelisted-ips non-empty or whitelisted-vcns non-empty, and, after normalising every entry — top-level whitelisted-ips plus each VCN entry's nested whitelisted-ips — to a CIDR, no single entry has prefix length 0 and the interval-merged union of all entries does not cover the entire IPv4 (or IPv6) address space. A null or absent network-endpoint-details is a FAIL. Whether the surviving narrower ranges are the organisation's approved networks is the Manual overlay, stated separately from this mechanical rule.
controls.remediation: Restrict the endpoint with `oci analytics analytics-instance change-network-endpoint --analytics-instance-id <ocid> --network-endpoint-details file://endpoint.json`, listing only approved CIDRs under whitelistedIps and internal VCNs under whitelistedVcns with narrow nested whitelistedIps, or migrate the instance to a PRIVATE endpoint bound to a subnet and to NSGs whose ingress rules name specific sources.
controls.caveat: Manual because judging whether the listed IPs and VCNs are the organisation's own approved networks is a business decision no API answers — a long whitelist of partner or ISP ranges passes the mechanical rule while leaving the console broadly reachable. Five traps. (1) "No entry equal to 0.0.0.0/0" is not a sufficient test: a complementary pair of /1 halves (the low half plus the high half), or a handful of /8s, covers the whole internet without matching any /0 string, so the check must be prefix-length-0 detection plus an interval-merge union over the address space. (2) A whitelisted-vcns entry carries its own nested whitelisted-ips, so a permissive sub-list inside an otherwise internal-looking VCN entry is real exposure and nested entries must be walked. (3) A null or absent network-endpoint-details is unrestricted access, not "unset", and must fail rather than skip. (4) A stopped (INACTIVE) instance still holds its endpoint configuration and counts. (5) A PRIVATE instance still depends on the NSGs in network-security-group-ids, so a private endpoint fronted by an internet-open NSG is only nominally restricted and the NSG rules must be fetched — NSG metadata alone never carries them. OAC instances are regional and compartment-scoped, so both loops are mandatory.

controls.title: Bind serverless Autonomous Databases to a private endpoint or an enforced access ACL
controls.objective: Serverless Autonomous Database endpoints are internet-facing by default, so every such database must either sit behind a VCN private endpoint or enforce a network access control list that names the permitted sources.
controls.procedure: For every compartment (`oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all`; `--include-root` is a valueless flag and ANY rather than ACCESSIBLE keeps indirectly-visible compartments in the tree) and every subscribed region from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy_ocid>`, run `oci db autonomous-database list --compartment-id <c> --all --region <region>`; or resolve tenancy-wide via `oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query AutonomousDatabase resources" --region <region> --all` then `oci db autonomous-database get`. Select the in-scope serverless population with the boolean `is-dedicated == false` — do NOT filter on infrastructure-type, whose documented values are CLOUD and CLOUD_AT_CUSTOMER, never SHARED/DEDICATED; a SHARED filter matches nothing and evaluates zero databases. Use infrastructure-type only as an additional filter if Exadata Cloud@Customer estates are to be excluded. For each selected database read subnet-id, private-endpoint-ip, nsg-ids, is-access-control-enabled and the whitelisted-ips array.
api: oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all
oci search resource-type list --region <region>  # confirm AutonomousDatabase is an indexed type before relying on Search
oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query AutonomousDatabase resources" --region <region> --all
controls.evidence: Per database OCID: is-dedicated (the attribute that actually separates serverless from dedicated), infrastructure-type, lifecycle-state, subnet-id and private-endpoint-ip, nsg-ids, is-access-control-enabled and the whitelisted-ips array, all from `oci db autonomous-database get`, with compartment-id and region. Record the count of databases returned by the list call and the count that survived the is-dedicated filter, so a filter that matched nothing is visible as an enumeration failure rather than as a clean tenancy.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when every autonomous database with is-dedicated == false and lifecycle-state not in {TERMINATED, TERMINATING, UNAVAILABLE} either has a non-null subnet-id (private endpoint), or has is-access-control-enabled == true together with a non-empty whitelisted-ips containing no entry that is 0.0.0.0/0 or otherwise of prefix length 0, and whose entries do not union to cover the whole address space. A database whose whitelisted-ips is populated while is-access-control-enabled is false is a FAIL. A run in which the serverless filter selected zero databases while the list call returned some is inconclusive, not a PASS.
controls.remediation: Apply an ACL with `oci db autonomous-database update --autonomous-database-id <ocid> --is-access-control-enabled true --whitelisted-ips '["<cidr>","<vcn_ocid>;<cidr>"]' --force` (the boolean must be set in the same change, since the list alone has no effect; `--force` suppresses the list-overwrite prompt), or move the database onto a private endpoint by supplying --subnet-id and --nsg-ids so it is reachable only from the VCN.
controls.caveat: Manual because whether the listed CIDRs are legitimate corporate sources cannot be settled by API. The catastrophic false pass is scoping the population by the wrong attribute: infrastructure-type on an Autonomous Database takes CLOUD or CLOUD_AT_CUSTOMER, not SHARED, so a SHARED filter silently selects zero databases and the entire tenancy scores PASS with no database ever examined — filter on is-dedicated == false and assert a non-zero selected count wherever the list call returned rows. The second sharpest is a populated whitelisted-ips with is-access-control-enabled == false: the list persists as stale configuration while the database stays open, so the boolean must be checked, not the array alone. Also: entries may be raw CIDRs, bare IPs, or VCN-scoped forms like "<vcn_ocid>;<cidr>", and each shape needs its own parser before any prefix-length or union test can run; a set of narrow-looking entries can still union to the whole internet, so test coverage of the address space rather than string-matching 0.0.0.0/0; dedicated Exadata databases (is-dedicated == true) are outside the control; mTLS being required (is-mtls-connection-required) is authentication, not network scope, and never substitutes for the ACL; a private endpoint is only as tight as the NSGs in nsg-ids; and ADBs are regional and compartment-scoped, so a home-region-only or root-only sweep under-reports.

controls.title: Force instances onto the authenticated v2 instance-metadata endpoint
controls.objective: The unauthenticated v1 metadata endpoint (http://169.254.169.254/opc/v1/) hands instance metadata, and any instance-principal credentials reachable through it, to anything that can make the instance issue an outbound HTTP request. Requiring v2, which demands an Authorization: Bearer Oracle header, turns a plain SSRF on a workload into a non-event instead of a credential leak.
controls.procedure: Loop over every subscribed region from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy_ocid>`. Per region, structured-search instance resources for all OCIDs tenancy-wide (`oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query instance resources where lifecycleState != 'TERMINATED'" --region <region> --all`; note the attribute is lifecycleState with a lower-case c — a misspelling silently matches nothing). If Search is denied or under-privileged, list compartments with `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all` (`--include-root` takes no value) and run `oci compute instance list --compartment-id <c> --all --region <region>` in each. For every non-terminated instance run `oci compute instance get --instance-id <ocid>` and read instance-options.are-legacy-imds-endpoints-disabled together with lifecycle-state and shape in the same projection. Then, over the same compartment set and the same region set, enumerate `oci compute-management instance-configuration list --compartment-id <c> --all --region <region>` and read instance-details.launch-details.instance-options.are-legacy-imds-endpoints-disabled on each, because these are what instance pools launch from.
api: oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query instance resources where lifecycleState != 'TERMINATED'" --region <region> --all
oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all
controls.evidence: instanceOptions.areLegacyImdsEndpointsDisabled from each GetInstance response, keyed by instance OCID, lifecycleState, compartment OCID and region, with an absent or null instanceOptions recorded explicitly as null rather than omitted; plus instanceDetails.launchDetails.instanceOptions.areLegacyImdsEndpointsDisabled from every GetInstanceConfiguration response, keyed by instance configuration OCID, compartment and region. Record the per-region instance count and instance-configuration count so an empty sweep is distinguishable from a compliant one.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS iff BOTH hold. (a) For every instance in every subscribed region whose lifecycleState is not TERMINATED or TERMINATING, instanceOptions.areLegacyImdsEndpointsDisabled == true. (b) For every instance configuration returned by `oci compute-management instance-configuration list` across every compartment in the subtree plus the tenancy root and every subscribed region, instanceDetails.launchDetails.instanceOptions.areLegacyImdsEndpointsDisabled == true. A null or absent instanceOptions block on either object is a FAIL, not a skip. Evidence is collected from instance configurations precisely because they are load-bearing — a tenancy whose running instances are all compliant but whose configurations still launch legacy IMDS reverts on the next scale or heal event and must not score PASS.
controls.remediation: Per instance: `oci compute instance update --instance-id <ocid> --instance-options '{"areLegacyImdsEndpointsDisabled": true}' --force` (no reboot needed; --force suppresses the complex-parameter overwrite prompt). Confirm the workload reads metadata via /opc/v2/ with header 'Authorization: Bearer Oracle' first, because flipping the flag breaks any code still calling v1. Then set the same field under instanceDetails.launchDetails.instanceOptions in every instance configuration — creating a replacement configuration and repointing the instance pool at it, since instance configurations are effectively immutable — so pool scale-out does not reintroduce v1.
controls.caveat: Four false-pass traps. (1) Search and the compute APIs are regional: a single-region run silently reports 100% pass for a tenancy with instances elsewhere, and `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <ocid>` must be the source of every --region value. (2) Instances launched before the option existed return instanceOptions as null, which JSON-path tooling reads as 'not false' and scores as pass; null means v1 is live and is a FAIL. (3) Fixing running instances is not durable if the backing instance configuration still launches with v1 enabled, so an instance pool re-creates non-compliant instances after any scale or heal event — which is why the verdict quantifies over instance configurations as well as instances, rather than collecting configuration evidence and then ignoring it. (4) Structured search returns only summary attributes and never exposes instanceOptions, so the per-instance GetInstance call is mandatory; Search also returns only what the caller can inspect, so reconcile its count against the compartment walk before trusting a small result set. The query attribute is lifecycleState, not lifeCycleState — the wrong casing errors or matches nothing, which reads as a clean tenancy.

controls.title: Require UEFI Secure Boot on shielded-capable virtual machines
controls.objective: Secure Boot makes the instance firmware refuse boot components that are not signed by a trusted authority, which blocks bootkit and unsigned-kernel-module persistence surviving a reinstall of the OS. On OCI this is a shielded-instance platform setting fixed at launch, so it is either designed in or absent.
controls.procedure: Per subscribed region from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy_ocid>`, collect all instance OCIDs — `oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query instance resources where lifecycleState != 'TERMINATED'" --region <region> --all` (lower-case c in lifecycleState), or `oci compute instance list --compartment-id <c> --all --region <region>` over every compartment from `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all`. For each non-terminated instance run `oci compute instance get`: platform-config must exist and platform-config.is-secure-boot-enabled must be true. In the same projection capture shape and launch-options.firmware (UEFI_64 versus BIOS), since a BIOS instance cannot carry Secure Boot. Establish applicability per instance from the shape rather than from bare-metal-versus-VM: `oci compute shape list --compartment-id <c> --region <region>` returns platform-config-options, whose secure-boot-options block tells you whether that specific shape supports the setting. Check the same platform-config field under instance-details.launch-details in every instance configuration returned by `oci compute-management instance-configuration list --compartment-id <c> --all --region <region>`.
api: oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query instance resources where lifecycleState != 'TERMINATED'" --region <region> --all
oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all
oci compute shape list --compartment-id <compartment_ocid> --region <region>  # read platform-config-options.secure-boot-options to decide per-shape applicability
controls.evidence: platformConfig.isSecureBootEnabled == true in the GetInstance response for each instance OCID, recorded with lifecycleState, shape, launchOptions.firmware and region, and with a null platformConfig captured explicitly as null; the shape's platformConfigOptions.secureBootOptions from ListShapes as the applicability record for any instance claimed to be incapable; and instanceDetails.launchDetails.platformConfig.isSecureBootEnabled for each instance configuration, keyed by configuration OCID, compartment and region.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS iff BOTH hold. (a) Every non-terminated instance in every subscribed region returns a non-null platformConfig with isSecureBootEnabled == true. (b) Every instance configuration across every compartment and subscribed region sets instanceDetails.launchDetails.platformConfig.isSecureBootEnabled == true, so that pool scale-out cannot launch unshielded instances. platformConfig == null is a FAIL on either object and must not be auto-classified as not-applicable; where the shape genuinely does not support Secure Boot, the finding is recorded as a FAIL carrying the shape's platformConfigOptions.secureBootOptions as the exception evidence and a shape-migration note, never converted into a pass.
controls.remediation: Secure Boot is immutable after launch. Re-launch from a UEFI image on a shielded-capable shape: `oci compute instance launch ... --platform-config '{"type":"AMD_VM","isSecureBootEnabled":true,"isMeasuredBootEnabled":true,"isTrustedPlatformModuleEnabled":true}'` where type matches the shape family (AMD_VM / INTEL_VM for virtual machines, the corresponding BM platform type for bare metal shapes that support shielded instances), migrate data, then terminate the old instance. Set the same block under instanceDetails.launchDetails.platformConfig in a replacement instance configuration and repoint the instance pool at it.
controls.caveat: platformConfig is null on shapes and legacy VMs with no shielded-instance support, and the tempting reading of null as not-applicable converts the whole estate into a false pass; the honest result is a FAIL with a shape-migration note. Applicability is shape-dependent across BOTH families — shielded instances (Secure Boot, Measured Boot, TPM) are supported on selected bare metal shapes as well as VM shapes, and several BM shapes are in fact where Measured Boot and TPM are offered — so do not write bare metal off as categorically incapable, which turns real, remediable failures into permanent exceptions. The genuine exclusions are GPU, HPC and legacy shape generations, and the image must be UEFI rather than BIOS (visible as launchOptions.firmware). Decide applicability per instance from the shape's platformConfigOptions.secureBootOptions and cite the current Oracle shielded-instance supported-shape list in any exception note. Secure Boot cannot be toggled on a live instance, so remediation is a rebuild and any check that expects `oci compute instance update` to fix it will report perpetual drift. Finally, Secure Boot blocks unsigned third-party kernel modules, so enabling it estate-wide needs a functional test, not just an API flip — and remediating instances while leaving instance configurations unshielded reverts on the next pool event, which is why the verdict covers both.

controls.title: Encrypt the host-to-storage data path for boot and block volume attachments
controls.objective: Block Volume data is always encrypted at rest, but the iSCSI/paravirtualized traffic between the compute host and the storage service is only encrypted when in-transit encryption is switched on for the attachment. Without it, volume traffic crosses the substrate network unencrypted, so at-rest encryption alone does not cover the read/write path.
controls.procedure: Per subscribed region (`oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy_ocid>`) and per compartment (`oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all`; `--include-root` takes no value), list instances and, for each non-terminated one, run `oci compute instance get` and read launch-options.is-pv-encryption-in-transit-enabled. Do not stop there: enumerate attachments compartment by compartment rather than trying to reach them through an instance filter, because `oci compute volume-attachment list` requires --compartment-id and --instance-id is only a filter applied inside that compartment. Run `oci compute volume-attachment list --compartment-id <c> --all --region <region>` over every ACTIVE compartment in the subtree plus the tenancy root, then join the returned attachments to instances by instance-id; read is-pv-encryption-in-transit-enabled, attachment-type and lifecycle-state on every attachment in state ATTACHED. Evidence the boot volume as a first-class object too: loop the ADs from `oci iam availability-domain list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --region <region>` and run `oci compute boot-volume-attachment list --compartment-id <c> --availability-domain <ad> --region <region>` (both parameters are required), asserting is-pv-encryption-in-transit-enabled == true on each BootVolumeAttachment in state ATTACHED. Finally check launch-options.is-pv-encryption-in-transit-enabled under instance-details.launch-details in every instance configuration.
api: oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy_ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --include-root --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all
oci compute volume-attachment list --compartment-id <compartment_ocid> --all --region <region>  # iterate every compartment; --instance-id is only an in-compartment filter
oci compute boot-volume-attachment list --compartment-id <compartment_ocid> --availability-domain <availability_domain> --region <region>  # both parameters required
oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query instance resources where lifecycleState != 'TERMINATED'" --region <region> --all
controls.evidence: launchOptions.isPvEncryptionInTransitEnabled from GetInstance per instance OCID (with shape and lifecycleState); isPvEncryptionInTransitEnabled, attachmentType and lifecycleState from every VolumeAttachment returned by ListVolumeAttachments across all compartments, each recorded with the instanceId it joins to and the compartment it was found in (which may differ from the instance's compartment); isPvEncryptionInTransitEnabled and lifecycleState from every BootVolumeAttachment returned by ListBootVolumeAttachments per compartment and availability domain; and instanceDetails.launchDetails.launchOptions.isPvEncryptionInTransitEnabled per instance configuration. All keyed by region, compartment and availability domain, with the compartment and AD lists actually swept recorded alongside so an incomplete enumeration is visible.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS iff all of the following hold. (a) For every non-terminated instance, launchOptions.isPvEncryptionInTransitEnabled == true. (b) Every VolumeAttachment in lifecycleState ATTACHED, joined by instance-id to a non-terminated instance, has isPvEncryptionInTransitEnabled == true. (c) Every BootVolumeAttachment in lifecycleState ATTACHED has isPvEncryptionInTransitEnabled == true. (d) Every instance configuration sets instanceDetails.launchDetails.launchOptions.isPvEncryptionInTransitEnabled == true, so pool scale-out does not launch unencrypted paths. Any false or null value on any of these objects is a FAIL. A result computed without sweeping every ACTIVE compartment (for volume attachments) and every availability domain (for boot volume attachments) is inconclusive, not a PASS.
controls.remediation: Stop the instance, then `oci compute instance update --instance-id <ocid> --launch-options '{"isPvEncryptionInTransitEnabled":true}' --force` and start it. For each data volume, detach and re-attach encrypted: `oci compute volume-attachment attach --type paravirtualized --instance-id <ocid> --volume-id <ocid> --is-pv-encryption-in-transit-enabled true`. Boot volumes take the setting from the instance launch, so a non-compliant BootVolumeAttachment is fixed by the stop/update/start above or by relaunching the instance. Set the same flag in the launch details of every instance configuration and repoint the pool at the replacement configuration.
controls.caveat: Checking only the instance launchOptions is the classic false pass: that flag governs the boot volume path, while each attached block volume carries its own isPvEncryptionInTransitEnabled and can be unencrypted on an otherwise compliant instance. The stated fix of 'run the attachment query with the instance filter' does not work — `oci compute volume-attachment list` requires --compartment-id and --instance-id is only a filter applied within that compartment, so an attachment created in a compartment other than the one being queried is still missed; the enumeration must iterate every ACTIVE compartment in the subtree plus the tenancy root and join attachments to instances by instance-id afterwards. The boot volume must also be evidenced directly through ListBootVolumeAttachments, which requires BOTH --compartment-id and --availability-domain, so the AD loop is mandatory and a missing AD silently drops every boot volume in it. In-transit encryption requires paravirtualized attachment on supported shapes with Oracle-provided or UEFI-capable images; shapes that cannot set it should be reported as evidenced exceptions rather than silently skipped. The instance-level change needs a stop/start, so an update that returns 200 while the instance keeps running is not yet in effect and re-reading the API can show true before the data path actually changes. Finally, remediating instances while the backing instance configurations still launch with the flag off reverts on the next scale or heal event, which is why instance configurations are in the verdict and not merely collected.

controls.title: Require a default tag to be stamped automatically onto newly created resources
controls.objective: Every resource created in the tenancy should inherit an automatically applied defined tag so that ownership, cost and incident attribution work without relying on operators to tag by hand.
controls.procedure: Work against the tenancy home region, because tag namespaces, tag definitions and tag defaults are IAM (home-region) objects. Resolve the tenancy OCID, then enumerate compartments with `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all` (`--include-root` is a valueless CLI flag; passing it a value aborts the call, and `--access-level ACCESSIBLE` silently truncates the tree for an auditor principal). Run `oci iam tag-default list --compartment-id <ocid> --all` for the tenancy root first, then for each child compartment. For every returned tag default read `tag-definition-id`, `is-required`, `value` and `lifecycle-state`, then confirm the owning namespace and definition are live: `oci iam tag-namespace get --tag-namespace-id <ocid>` and `oci iam tag get --tag-namespace-id <ocid> --tag-name <name>` must both return `is-retired: false`.
api: oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all
controls.evidence: The tag-default list response for the tenancy root compartment: at least one item with lifecycle-state ACTIVE, `is-required: true`, a non-empty `value`, and a `tag-definition-id` whose tag definition and owning namespace both report `is-retired: false`. Record the child-compartment tag-default listings as well, plus the compartment count returned by the subtree walk so a truncated tree is visible in the evidence.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when `oci iam tag-default list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --all` returns >=1 entry with lifecycle-state ACTIVE and `is-required: true` whose tag definition and tag namespace both have `is-retired: false`. An empty list, only `is-required: false` entries, or an entry whose namespace or definition is retired is a FAIL. A tag default set on the root is inherited by descendant compartments, so root-level evidence is sufficient for this verdict; if the organisation requires per-compartment values instead, tighten the rule to demand a qualifying ACTIVE, is-required tag default in every ACTIVE compartment returned by the subtree listing.
controls.remediation: Create a defined tag namespace and key in the root compartment (`oci iam tag-namespace create`, `oci iam tag create`), then bind it as a default: `oci iam tag-default create --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --tag-definition-id <ocid> --value <default-value> --is-required true`. Add equivalent defaults in child compartments only where a different enforced value is required, since the root default already propagates down the tree. Never retire a namespace or definition that a live tag default references.
controls.caveat: A retired namespace or a retired tag definition leaves the tag default present in the API response but completely inert, which is the primary false pass here: the record must be resolved through `tag-namespace get` and `tag get` rather than trusted from the tag-default listing alone. Tag defaults never retro-tag resources that already exist, so a passing verdict says nothing about the existing estate. These are IAM objects served from the home region, so issuing the calls against another region returns nothing and reads as an empty result rather than an error.

controls.title: An alert destination exists and a subscriber has confirmed receipt
controls.objective: Detective controls are worthless if nothing delivers the alert. The tenancy needs a live Notifications topic with a subscription that has actually been confirmed, so Events and Alarms have somewhere to publish.
controls.procedure: Loop over subscribed regions from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`. Build the compartment set once with `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all`. In each region, for each compartment, run `oci ons topic list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>` and `oci ons subscription list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>`. For each subscription read `topic-id`, `protocol`, `endpoint` and `lifecycle-state`, and join it back to a topic whose `lifecycle-state` is ACTIVE in the same region.
api: oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all
controls.evidence: A topic object with lifecycle-state ACTIVE plus at least one subscription object whose `topic-id` matches it and whose `lifecycle-state` is ACTIVE (not PENDING); record topic OCID, topic compartment OCID, subscription OCID, protocol, endpoint and region for each pair, together with the list of regions enumerated.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when at least one ONS topic with lifecycle-state ACTIVE exists in the tenancy and at least one subscription referencing that topic, in the same region, has lifecycle-state ACTIVE. A topic with zero subscriptions, or with only PENDING subscriptions, is a FAIL; so is a run that enumerated fewer regions than `region-subscription list` returned.
controls.remediation: `oci ons topic create --name sec-alerts --compartment-id <ocid> --region <r>` then `oci ons subscription create --topic-id <ocid> --protocol EMAIL --subscription-endpoint <mailbox> --compartment-id <ocid> --region <r>`, and have the recipient click the confirmation link so the state moves from PENDING to ACTIVE. Create one topic per subscribed region that carries Events rules, since a rule can only publish to a topic in its own region. Prefer a distribution list or a chat/paging endpoint over one person's mailbox.
controls.caveat: Two false-pass traps. First, EMAIL subscriptions sit in PENDING until the recipient confirms, and a PENDING subscription silently drops every message, so counting subscriptions instead of testing `lifecycle-state == ACTIVE` passes a dead channel. Second, ONS is regional and compartment-scoped: a topic in the home region does nothing for Events rules created in another region, and a root-compartment-only listing (or a compartment walk run with `--access-level ACCESSIBLE` under a partially privileged principal) misses topics parked in a child compartment. Deliverability itself (mailbox exists, filters do not bin it, the paging integration is live) cannot be proven from the API and needs an out-of-band test message.

controls.title: Alert when federation providers are added, altered, or removed
controls.objective: Adding or editing an identity provider changes who can obtain a session in the tenancy. Those events must reach a human in near-real time, not surface weeks later in an audit export.
controls.procedure: Work in the tenancy home region (resolve it from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`, where `is-home-region` is true). List rules across the compartment tree: `oci events rule list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <home>` for the tenancy root and each ACTIVE compartment. For each rule run `oci events rule get --rule-id <ocid>` and parse the `condition` JSON for eventType entries `com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createidentityprovider`, `.updateidentityprovider`, `.deleteidentityprovider`. Record the rule's own `compartment-id`, confirm `is-enabled` is true, and confirm at least one action of type ONS with `is-enabled: true` whose topic passes the 4.2 delivery check.
controls.evidence: The rule OCID and its `compartment-id`, the `condition` string listing the three identityprovider eventTypes, `is-enabled: true`, and an `actions.actions[]` entry with action-type ONS, `is-enabled: true`, and a topic-id resolving to an ACTIVE topic with a subscription in lifecycle-state ACTIVE.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when an Events rule whose `compartment-id` equals the tenancy OCID (root compartment) exists in the home region with `is-enabled: true`, a condition matching all three of createidentityprovider, updateidentityprovider and deleteidentityprovider, and an ONS action whose own `is-enabled` is true pointing at a topic with >=1 subscription in lifecycle-state ACTIVE. A matching rule anchored in a child compartment does not satisfy this control, because an Events rule only observes its own compartment and that compartment's descendants.
controls.remediation: `oci events rule create --region <home> --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --display-name idp-changes --is-enabled true --condition '{"eventType":["com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createidentityprovider","com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateidentityprovider","com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deleteidentityprovider"]}' --actions '{"actions":[{"actionType":"ONS","isEnabled":true,"topicId":"<ocid>"}]}'`
controls.caveat: Identity control-plane events are emitted only in the tenancy home region, so a correct rule built in any other region never fires while looking valid. Test the whole chain: a rule can be enabled while its ONS action has `isEnabled: false`, or point at a topic whose only subscription is PENDING, and a rule created below the root observes only its own subtree. In tenancies migrated to identity domains, IdP objects live inside a domain (enumerate with `oci iam domain list` and the domain's own admin surface) and may emit domain-scoped event types, so a rule matching only the legacy identitycontrolplane types can be a false pass; corroborate against the domain's event configuration.

controls.title: Alert when federated-group-to-IAM-group mappings are altered
controls.objective: Group mappings decide which federated users land in which privileged IAM groups. Silently repointing a mapping is a stealthy privilege grant, so every create, update and delete must raise a notification.
controls.procedure: In the home region, list Events rules for the tenancy root and every ACTIVE compartment (`oci events rule list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <home>`), fetch each with `oci events rule get --rule-id <ocid>`, and search the `condition` JSON for `com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createidpgroupmapping`, `.updateidpgroupmapping` and `.deleteidpgroupmapping`. Record each rule's own `compartment-id` and `is-enabled`, then follow each ONS action (which must itself have `is-enabled: true`) through `oci ons topic get --topic-id <ocid>` and `oci ons subscription list` to prove a live delivery path. Enumerate current mappings for context with `oci iam identity-provider list` followed by `oci iam idp-group-mapping list --identity-provider-id <ocid> --all`.
controls.evidence: Rule OCID and its `compartment-id`, the `condition` containing the three idpgroupmapping eventTypes, `is-enabled: true` on the rule, and an ONS action with `is-enabled: true` whose topic has a subscription in lifecycle-state ACTIVE.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when an Events rule whose `compartment-id` equals the tenancy OCID (root compartment) exists in the home region, is enabled, matches createidpgroupmapping, updateidpgroupmapping and deleteidpgroupmapping, and routes through an enabled ONS action to a topic with at least one ACTIVE subscription. A rule in a child compartment, or an enabled rule whose ONS action is disabled, FAILs.
controls.remediation: `oci events rule create --region <home> --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --display-name idp-group-mapping-changes --is-enabled true --condition '{"eventType":["com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createidpgroupmapping","com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateidpgroupmapping","com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deleteidpgroupmapping"]}' --actions '{"actions":[{"actionType":"ONS","isEnabled":true,"topicId":"<ocid>"}]}'`
controls.caveat: Home-region-only emission applies here as well, and a rule anchored below the tenancy root sees only its own subtree. The bigger trap is identity domains: mappings for a domain-based IdP are managed through the domain's own admin/SCIM surface and do not necessarily produce the legacy identitycontrolplane idpgroupmapping events, so a migrated tenancy can hold a syntactically perfect, enabled rule that never fires. Where domains are in use (enumerate them with `oci iam domain list`), corroborate against the domain's event configuration instead of trusting the rule alone.

controls.title: Group membership changes reach an alerting channel
controls.objective: Because authorization in OCI is granted to groups, creating or deleting a group is a change to the permission model itself and should generate an alert carrying the actor's identity.
controls.procedure: Home region only. For the tenancy root and each ACTIVE compartment run `oci events rule list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <home>`, then `oci events rule get --rule-id <ocid>` and inspect `condition` for `com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.creategroup`, `.updategroup` and `.deletegroup`. Record the rule's `compartment-id`; require `is-enabled: true`, an ONS action whose own `is-enabled` is true, and a topic that resolves to an ACTIVE topic with an ACTIVE subscription. Where the tenancy's realm exposes them, treat the membership event types (`...addusertogroup`, `...removeuserfromgroup`) as an additional strengthening — verify which virtualnetwork/identity event types exist before pinning them into a condition. Baseline the group set with `oci iam group list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --all`, plus `oci identity-domains groups list --endpoint <domain-url> --all` for each domain returned by `oci iam domain list`.
controls.evidence: Rule OCID with its `compartment-id`, the `condition` JSON listing the three group eventTypes, `is-enabled: true` on the rule, and the ONS action (`is-enabled: true`) topic-id with its subscription lifecycle-state ACTIVE.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when an enabled Events rule whose `compartment-id` equals the tenancy OCID exists in the home region, matches creategroup, updategroup and deletegroup, and delivers through an enabled ONS action to a topic having >=1 subscription in lifecycle-state ACTIVE. A child-compartment rule, a disabled ONS action, or a PENDING-only subscription FAILs.
controls.remediation: `oci events rule create --region <home> --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --display-name iam-group-changes --is-enabled true --condition '{"eventType":["com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.creategroup","com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updategroup","com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletegroup"]}' --actions '{"actions":[{"actionType":"ONS","isEnabled":true,"topicId":"<ocid>"}]}'`. Add the membership event types to the same condition where the realm emits them, and pair the rule with a scheduled Logging Search over the audit subtree pseudo-log for group-membership API calls.
controls.caveat: Matching group create/update/delete does not cover adding a user to an existing privileged group, which is a distinct event type; treating this control as full group-membership monitoring is the classic false sense of coverage, so pair it with an audit query over `search "<tenancy-ocid>/_Audit_Include_Subcompartment"` for the membership API calls. Identity events are home-region only and a rule anchored in a child compartment gives no tenancy-wide coverage. In identity-domain tenancies groups are domain objects (listed with the plural `oci identity-domains groups list`, not the singular form) and the legacy event types may not be raised, so verify against a real change if you need certainty.

controls.title: Alert whenever authorization policies are written, edited, or deleted
controls.objective: An IAM policy statement is the only thing between a principal and a resource. Any change to the policy corpus must be visible immediately so an over-broad grant cannot sit unnoticed.
controls.procedure: In the home region, enumerate Events rules for the tenancy root and every ACTIVE compartment with `oci events rule list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <home>` and read each via `oci events rule get --rule-id <ocid>`. Look in `condition` for `com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createpolicy`, `.updatepolicy` and `.deletepolicy`. Record the rule's `compartment-id`, verify `is-enabled: true`, and verify the ONS action's own `is-enabled` is true and its topic-id passes the 4.2 delivery check. Baseline the policy corpus per compartment with `oci iam policy list --compartment-id <ocid> --all`, driving the compartment set from `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all`.
api: oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all
controls.evidence: The rule OCID and `compartment-id`, its `condition` containing createpolicy, updatepolicy and deletepolicy, `is-enabled: true`, and an ONS action with `is-enabled: true` pointing at a topic with an ACTIVE subscription.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when an enabled Events rule whose `compartment-id` equals the tenancy OCID exists in the home region, matches all three policy eventTypes, and routes through an enabled ONS action to a topic with >=1 subscription in lifecycle-state ACTIVE. A rule found only in a child compartment FAILs, since it observes just that subtree.
controls.remediation: `oci events rule create --region <home> --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --display-name iam-policy-changes --is-enabled true --condition '{"eventType":["com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createpolicy","com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updatepolicy","com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletepolicy"]}' --actions '{"actions":[{"actionType":"ONS","isEnabled":true,"topicId":"<ocid>"}]}'`
controls.caveat: Policies can be attached in any compartment but the event surfaces in the home region, so build and check the rule there and require it at the root: a rule created in a leaf compartment only observes that compartment and its children. Confirm the ONS action itself is enabled, since a disabled action inside an enabled rule is the most common silent failure. Running the compartment walk with `--access-level ACCESSIBLE` under a partially privileged auditor principal can drop compartments from the policy baseline without any error.

controls.title: Alert on IAM principal lifecycle and capability changes
controls.objective: Creating a user, re-enabling a disabled one, or granting API-key and auth-token capabilities are all persistence moves, so they must generate an alert while the account is still fresh.
controls.procedure: Home region. Walk the tenancy root and each ACTIVE compartment with `oci events rule list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <home>` and `oci events rule get --rule-id <ocid>`; parse `condition` for `com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createuser`, `.updateuser`, `.deleteuser`, and ideally `.updateusercapabilities` and `.updateuserstate`. Record the rule's `compartment-id`, require `is-enabled: true` on both the rule and its ONS action, and resolve the topic. Baseline the user population with `oci iam user list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --all` for legacy IAM, and for identity-domain tenancies resolve each domain's `url` from `oci iam domain list --compartment-id <ocid> --all` (repeat across compartments) and enumerate with the plural list form `oci identity-domains users list --endpoint <domain-url> --all`; the singular `oci identity-domains user` noun carries only single-user get/create/put/patch/delete and fails with a usage error on `list`.
controls.evidence: Rule OCID and `compartment-id`, the `condition` listing the user eventTypes (createuser, updateuser, deleteuser at minimum), `is-enabled: true`, the ONS action's `is-enabled: true` and topic-id with a confirmed (ACTIVE) subscription, plus the per-domain user counts from `oci identity-domains users list`.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when an enabled Events rule whose `compartment-id` equals the tenancy OCID exists in the home region, matches createuser, updateuser and deleteuser, and delivers through an ONS action with `is-enabled: true` to a topic with >=1 ACTIVE subscription; capability and state event types are a strengthening, not a requirement. A child-compartment rule or a disabled ONS action FAILs.
controls.remediation: `oci events rule create --region <home> --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --display-name iam-user-changes --is-enabled true --condition '{"eventType":["com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createuser","com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateuser","com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deleteuser","com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateusercapabilities","com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateuserstate"]}' --actions '{"actions":[{"actionType":"ONS","isEnabled":true,"topicId":"<ocid>"}]}'`. In identity-domain tenancies additionally configure the domain's own notification/event delivery for user lifecycle changes.
controls.caveat: The state that matters may not be where you are looking. In an identity-domain tenancy users are domain objects reachable only through the domain endpoint via the plural `oci identity-domains users list --endpoint <domain-url> --all`, and legacy identitycontrolplane user events may not be emitted for them, so a rule that passes this check can still be blind to every real account creation. Identity events are home-region only, and a rule below the tenancy root covers only its own subtree. `updateuser` also fires on benign profile edits, so teams often disable the ONS action while leaving the rule enabled; check both flags.

controls.title: Alert on creation, modification, or deletion of virtual cloud networks
controls.objective: A new or altered VCN can introduce an entirely new ingress path into the tenancy, so network topology changes should notify the security team rather than being discovered at the next review.
controls.procedure: VCN events are regional. For every region returned by `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>` — not merely the regions that currently hold networking — run `oci events rule list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>` for the tenancy root and each ACTIVE compartment, then `oci events rule get --rule-id <ocid>`, matching `condition` on `com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createvcn`, `.updatevcn` and `.deletevcn`. Record each rule's `compartment-id`, require `is-enabled: true` on the rule and on its ONS action, and confirm the referenced topic lives in the same region with an ACTIVE subscription. Use `oci network vcn list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>` only as reporting context for which regions are currently populated.
api: oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query vcn resources where lifecycleState = 'AVAILABLE'" --region <region> --all
controls.evidence: Per subscribed region: a rule OCID with `compartment-id` equal to the tenancy OCID whose `condition` lists createvcn, updatevcn and deletevcn, with `is-enabled: true` and an ONS action (`is-enabled: true`) whose topic resolves in that same region and has a subscription in lifecycle-state ACTIVE. Also record the region list itself and the current VCN inventory per region as context.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when, for every region returned by `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`, an Events rule in that region's root (tenancy) compartment has `is-enabled: true`, matches createvcn, updatevcn and deletevcn, and routes to an ONS action with `is-enabled: true` whose topic is in the same region and has >=1 ACTIVE subscription. Current VCN inventory must never be used to excuse a region: an unmonitored empty region is exactly where a `createvcn` needs to be caught.
controls.remediation: In each subscribed region: `oci events rule create --region <r> --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --display-name vcn-changes --is-enabled true --condition '{"eventType":["com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createvcn","com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatevcn","com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletevcn"]}' --actions '{"actions":[{"actionType":"ONS","isEnabled":true,"topicId":"<regional-topic-ocid>"}]}'`, creating a same-region ONS topic first. Bake the rule into the region-enablement runbook so a newly subscribed region is never left uncovered.
controls.caveat: This is where single-region checking produces the loudest false pass: Events rules and ONS topics are both regional, so a perfect rule in one region gives zero coverage for a VCN built in another, and scoping the verdict to regions that already contain VCNs makes the result flip over time while leaving the empty regions — the interesting ones — unwatched. The rule's ONS action must target a topic in the same region as the rule and must itself be enabled. A rule created in a child compartment only observes that subtree, so tenancy-wide coverage requires the rule in the root compartment of each subscribed region. Note that `oci search` is itself a regional call and must be looped; its query attribute is `lifecycleState`, not `lifeCycleState`.

controls.title: Alert on routing-table modifications inside VCNs
controls.objective: Route table edits can silently redirect traffic through an attacker-controlled appliance or open a path to the internet through a NAT or DRG, so these changes must be announced when they happen.
controls.procedure: For each region from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>` and for the tenancy root plus each ACTIVE compartment, list and fetch Events rules (`oci events rule list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>`, `oci events rule get --rule-id <ocid>`) and match `condition` against `com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createroutetable`, `.updateroutetable`, `.deleteroutetable` and, where used, `.changeroutetablecompartment`. Record the rule's `compartment-id`, confirm `is-enabled: true` on the rule and on its ONS action, and confirm the topic is in the same region with an ACTIVE subscription. Inventory route tables for context with `oci network route-table list --compartment-id <ocid> --vcn-id <ocid> --all --region <r>`.
controls.evidence: Rule OCID, its `compartment-id`, region, the `condition` containing the route-table eventTypes, `is-enabled: true`, and the ONS action (`is-enabled: true`) topic-id with subscription lifecycle-state ACTIVE.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when, in every subscribed region, an Events rule whose `compartment-id` equals the tenancy OCID (or, for a deliberately decentralised design, a rule set whose compartments together cover every compartment that can hold a route table) is enabled, matches createroutetable, updateroutetable and deleteroutetable, and delivers through an enabled ONS action to a same-region ONS topic with >=1 ACTIVE subscription.
controls.remediation: Per region: `oci events rule create --region <r> --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --display-name route-table-changes --is-enabled true --condition '{"eventType":["com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createroutetable","com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updateroutetable","com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deleteroutetable","com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changeroutetablecompartment"]}' --actions '{"actions":[{"actionType":"ONS","isEnabled":true,"topicId":"<ocid>"}]}'`. Pair it with a scheduled Logging Search over `search "<tenancy-ocid>/_Audit_Include_Subcompartment"` for UpdateRouteTable so the alert can be correlated with the actual route change.
controls.caveat: Two scoping traps rather than one. Regionally, check every subscribed region, not just the home region or the regions that currently hold VCNs. By compartment, an Events rule only observes its own compartment and that compartment's descendants, so a rule anchored below the root leaves route-table changes in sibling compartments unalerted while satisfying a naive presence check — capture the rule's `compartment-id` as evidence. The update event fires on the table object and carries no before/after route detail, so the alert proves detection exists but never establishes whether the change was dangerous, which is why it must be paired with an audit-subtree query.

controls.title: Subnet firewall edits reach an alerting channel
controls.objective: Security lists are the stateful firewall for a subnet, and loosening one to 0.0.0.0/0 is a one-command exposure, so create, update and delete on these objects must be alerted.
controls.procedure: Loop every subscribed region from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>` and, within each, the tenancy root plus every ACTIVE compartment. Run `oci events rule list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>` then `oci events rule get --rule-id <ocid>`; search `condition` for `com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createsecuritylist`, `.updatesecuritylist` and `.deletesecuritylist`. Record the rule's `compartment-id`, require `is-enabled: true` on the rule and on the ONS action, and require a same-region topic with an ACTIVE subscription. Use `oci network security-list list --compartment-id <ocid> --vcn-id <ocid> --all --region <r>` as inventory context only.
controls.evidence: The rule OCID with its `compartment-id` and region, the `condition` JSON with the three securitylist eventTypes, `is-enabled: true`, and an ONS action (`is-enabled: true`) whose topic has a confirmed ACTIVE subscription in the same region.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when, in every subscribed region, an enabled Events rule whose `compartment-id` equals the tenancy OCID matches createsecuritylist, updatesecuritylist and deletesecuritylist and publishes through an enabled ONS action to a same-region ONS topic with >=1 ACTIVE subscription. A rule in a child compartment, a disabled ONS action, a cross-region topic, or a region skipped because it holds no VCNs today all FAIL.
controls.remediation: Per region: `oci events rule create --region <r> --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --display-name security-list-changes --is-enabled true --condition '{"eventType":["com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createsecuritylist","com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatesecuritylist","com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletesecuritylist"]}' --actions '{"actions":[{"actionType":"ONS","isEnabled":true,"topicId":"<ocid>"}]}'`
controls.caveat: Security lists and network security groups are two different enforcement objects; a rule covering only security lists leaves NSG changes (control 4.11) unmonitored, and teams frequently assume one implies the other. Regional scoping must follow the subscription list rather than current inventory, and the rule must sit in the root compartment — an Events rule below the root observes only its own subtree, so record `compartment-id` in evidence. The default security list of a VCN is edited in place, so the event you see is updatesecuritylist with no indication of which rule changed; the notification proves detection exists, not that the change was reviewed.

controls.title: Security group edits reach an alerting channel
controls.objective: NSGs attach firewall rules directly to VNICs and are the preferred enforcement point in modern OCI designs, so their creation, modification and deletion must surface as security-relevant events.
controls.procedure: For each subscribed region and for the tenancy root plus each ACTIVE compartment run `oci events rule list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>`, then `oci events rule get --rule-id <ocid>` and match `condition` on `com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createnetworksecuritygroup`, `.updatenetworksecuritygroup` and `.deletenetworksecuritygroup`. Record the rule's `compartment-id`, verify `is-enabled: true` on rule and ONS action, and verify the topic is same-region with a confirmed subscription. Then settle the rule-member question deterministically instead of leaving it open: enumerate the virtualnetwork event types the tenancy's realm actually emits (Events service reference plus `oci events rule create --generate-param-json-input condition`, corroborated by a live test that adds and removes a throwaway rule in a scratch NSG and observes what is delivered). If rule-member event types exist, add them to the required condition; if they do not, require the compensating audit query described in the remediation. Enumerate NSGs via `oci network nsg list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>` and their rules via `oci network nsg rules list --nsg-id <ocid> --all`.
controls.evidence: Rule OCID, `compartment-id` and region, the `condition` listing the three networksecuritygroup eventTypes (plus any rule-member event types the realm emits), `is-enabled: true`, and the ONS action (`is-enabled: true`) topic-id with an ACTIVE subscription. Where rule-member events do not exist, the saved Logging Search query and its most recent result set stand as the compensating evidence.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when, in every subscribed region, an enabled Events rule whose `compartment-id` equals the tenancy OCID matches createnetworksecuritygroup, updatenetworksecuritygroup and deletenetworksecuritygroup and delivers through an enabled ONS action to a same-region ONS topic with >=1 ACTIVE subscription AND changes to the rule members of an existing NSG are covered — either by the realm's rule-member event types included in the same condition, or by a scheduled audit query on the NSG security-rule API calls. Object-lifecycle coverage alone, with no rule-member coverage of any kind, FAILs.
