controls.remediation: Per region: `oci events rule create --region <r> --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --display-name nsg-changes --is-enabled true --condition '{"eventType":["com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createnetworksecuritygroup","com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatenetworksecuritygroup","com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletenetworksecuritygroup"]}' --actions '{"actions":[{"actionType":"ONS","isEnabled":true,"topicId":"<ocid>"}]}'`. Where the realm emits rule-member event types, append them to the same eventType array. Otherwise add the compensating detection: `oci logging-search search-logs --search-query "search \"<tenancy-ocid>/_Audit_Include_Subcompartment\" | where data.request.action = 'POST' and (data.eventName = 'AddNetworkSecurityGroupSecurityRules' or data.eventName = 'UpdateNetworkSecurityGroupSecurityRules' or data.eventName = 'RemoveNetworkSecurityGroupSecurityRules')" --time-start <t0> --time-end <t1> --region <r>` on a schedule that publishes to the same ONS topic.
controls.caveat: These event types cover the NSG object, not its rule members: adding a 0.0.0.0/0 ingress rule to an existing NSG is the highest-value change and is the one most likely to go unalerted. Do not leave that as an open question for the assessor — establish empirically whether rule-member event types exist in the tenancy's realm and, if they do not, require the audit-log compensating query and mark object-only coverage as a FAIL. Note the audit query must use the subtree pseudo-log `_Audit_Include_Subcompartment`; the plain `_Audit` log returns root-compartment events only and will report zero NSG rule changes in a tenancy whose workloads live in child compartments. Regional and compartment scoping apply exactly as in 4.8-4.10: the rule belongs in the root compartment, one per subscribed region, with the ONS topic co-located.

controls.title: Attaching or detaching an edge gateway reaches an alerting channel
controls.objective: Gateways are the doors between a VCN and everything outside it, so attaching an internet or NAT gateway, or standing up a DRG, changes the tenancy's exposure and must trigger a notification.
controls.procedure: For each region from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>` and for the tenancy root plus each ACTIVE compartment, fetch Events rules (`oci events rule list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>`; `oci events rule get --rule-id <ocid>`) and check `condition` for the create/update/delete triples of `com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.*` covering drg, drgattachment, internetgateway, natgateway, servicegateway and localpeeringgateway. Record the rule's `compartment-id`; require `is-enabled: true` on the rule and on its ONS action, and a same-region topic with an ACTIVE subscription. Inventory the gateway families actually present per region for reporting context, but never use that inventory to exempt a region.
controls.evidence: Rule OCID, `compartment-id` and region; the `condition` enumerating create, update and delete event types for drg, drgattachment, internetgateway, natgateway, servicegateway and localpeeringgateway; `is-enabled: true`; and an ONS action (`is-enabled: true`) whose topic has an ACTIVE subscription in the same region. Record the per-region gateway inventory alongside it.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when, for every subscribed region — and at a minimum every region that contains any of VCN, DRG, DRG attachment, internet gateway, NAT gateway, service gateway or local peering gateway — an Events rule in the tenancy root compartment of that region has `is-enabled: true`, matches create, update and delete for all six families, and delivers through an ONS action with `is-enabled: true` to a same-region topic with >=1 ACTIVE subscription. A rule covering only the internet gateway, a rule anchored in a child compartment, or a region excused because it holds no VCN today (a DRG is a standalone regional resource and needs none) all FAIL.
controls.remediation: Per region create one rule whose condition array includes com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.{create,update,delete} for drg, drgattachment, internetgateway, natgateway, servicegateway and localpeeringgateway, with an enabled ONS action: `oci events rule create --region <r> --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --display-name gateway-changes --is-enabled true --condition <json-with-all-six-families> --actions '{"actions":[{"actionType":"ONS","isEnabled":true,"topicId":"<same-region-topic-ocid>"}]}'`
controls.caveat: This control spans several distinct resource families, and the common partial implementation covers only the internet gateway, which passes a naive 'is there a gateway rule' check while leaving DRG, DRG attachment and NAT unmonitored; match every family explicitly in the condition. A DRG exists independently of any VCN, so scoping coverage to regions that currently contain a VCN exempts precisely the region where a new DRG would be stood up — drive the region loop from the subscription list. Regional co-location of the ONS topic, an enabled ONS action, and root-compartment anchoring apply as with the other networking event controls.

controls.title: Subnet traffic is recorded so an investigation has data to work from
controls.objective: Without flow logs there is no record of who talked to what inside the VCN, which makes lateral-movement investigation and exfiltration analysis impossible after the fact.
controls.procedure: Build the compartment set once with `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all` (`--include-root` takes no value). For every region from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`, enumerate subnets with `oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query subnet resources where lifecycleState = 'AVAILABLE'" --region <r> --all` (a regional call, repeated per region) or `oci network subnet list --compartment-id <ocid> --vcn-id <ocid> --all --region <r>`. Then enumerate logs across the whole compartment set, not just the subnet's own compartment: `oci logging log-group list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>` and `oci logging log list --log-group-id <ocid> --all --region <r>`. Match logs where `configuration.source.service` is flowlogs, `configuration.source.category` is all, and `configuration.source.resource` is the subnet OCID or its parent VCN OCID.
api: oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all
oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query subnet resources where lifecycleState = 'AVAILABLE'" --region <region> --all
controls.evidence: For each subnet OCID (with its VCN OCID, compartment and region): a log object with `lifecycle-state: ACTIVE`, `is-enabled: true`, `configuration.source.service: flowlogs`, `configuration.source.category: all`, and `configuration.source.resource` equal to that subnet OCID or its VCN OCID, plus the log's own OCID, log group and region. Record subnet counts per region so an empty enumeration is visible.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when every AVAILABLE subnet in every subscribed region is covered by a Logging log that is simultaneously `lifecycle-state: ACTIVE` and `is-enabled: true`, of service flowlogs and category all, whose `source.resource` is that subnet or its parent VCN and whose region matches the subnet's region. Any uncovered subnet is a FAIL; so is a region whose subnet enumeration returned zero while VCNs exist there, which indicates an enumeration failure rather than compliance.
controls.remediation: Create a log group then a flow log per subnet or per VCN: `oci logging log-group create --compartment-id <ocid> --display-name flowlogs --region <r>`; `oci logging log create --log-group-id <ocid> --display-name <subnet>-flow --log-type SERVICE --is-enabled true --retention-duration 90 --region <r> --configuration '{"compartmentId":"<ocid>","source":{"sourceType":"OCISERVICE","service":"flowlogs","resource":"<subnet-or-vcn-ocid>","category":"all"}}'`. Prefer VCN-level logs so new subnets inherit coverage, and set retention to at least the incident-investigation window.
controls.caveat: Four false-pass traps. (1) A log object can exist with `is-enabled: false` or lifecycle-state CREATING/FAILED, so presence is not coverage; test both fields. (2) Flow logging can be attached at the VCN level, which covers its subnets, so matching strictly on subnet OCIDs yields false FAILs while matching only VCNs misses subnets in VCNs without a parent-level log — accept either and record which. (3) Logs and subnets are both regional and compartment-scoped, and the log group usually lives in a central logging compartment different from the subnet's compartment, so the two enumerations must be joined tenancy-wide rather than per compartment, and the compartment walk must use `--access-level ANY` or it can silently drop the logging compartment. (4) The resource-search attribute is `lifecycleState`; a misspelt query returns nothing and a zero-subnet result then reads as a clean tenancy. Retention shorter than the investigation window is a real gap even on a pass.

controls.title: Cloud Guard observes the whole tenancy from the root compartment down
controls.objective: Cloud Guard is OCI's native posture and threat detection service; enabled at the tenancy root with recipes attached, it continuously flags misconfiguration and suspicious activity across every compartment.
controls.procedure: Run `oci cloud-guard configuration get --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid>` and read `status`, `reporting-region` and `self-manage-resources`. Then prove coverage exists across the whole tree, because targets can be created in child compartments: `oci cloud-guard target list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ACCESSIBLE --all` (the Cloud Guard access-level enum is ACCESSIBLE/RESTRICTED — `ANY` is not valid here). For each returned target run `oci cloud-guard target get --target-id <ocid>` and check that `target-resource-type` is COMPARTMENT, `target-resource-id` equals the tenancy OCID, `lifecycle-state` is ACTIVE, and the detector and responder recipe collections are non-empty. Inspect the target's effective detector rules (`oci cloud-guard target-detector-recipe list --target-id <ocid> --compartment-id <ocid> --all`) for rules that have been disabled or had their risk level lowered.
api: oci cloud-guard target list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ACCESSIBLE --all
controls.evidence: The configuration response with `status: ENABLED` and a populated `reporting-region`; plus a target object with `target-resource-type: COMPARTMENT`, `target-resource-id` equal to the tenancy root OCID, `lifecycle-state: ACTIVE`, the target's own compartment OCID, and its attached detector recipes together with the enabled/disabled state and risk level of their effective rules.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when Cloud Guard configuration `status` is ENABLED for the tenancy AND the subtree target listing contains at least one target with `lifecycle-state: ACTIVE` whose `target-resource-id` equals the tenancy root compartment OCID and which has >=1 attached detector recipe containing at least one rule with `is-enabled: true`. Status ENABLED with no target, with only child-compartment-scoped targets, or with a recipe whose entire rule set is disabled, all FAIL.
controls.remediation: `oci cloud-guard configuration update --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --status ENABLED --reporting-region <region>`, then create a root-scoped target: `oci cloud-guard target create --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --display-name tenancy-target --target-resource-type COMPARTMENT --target-resource-id <tenancy-ocid>` and attach the Oracle-managed configuration and activity detector recipes plus a responder recipe. Where cloned recipes are used, diff their rules against the Oracle-managed originals and re-enable anything switched off.
controls.caveat: `status: ENABLED` on its own is the false pass: the service can report enabled while every target has been deleted, or while the only target points at a child compartment, leaving sibling compartments unmonitored. Enumerating targets without `--compartment-id-in-subtree true` is the mirror-image error — it returns only targets whose own compartment is the root and can drive a FAIL on a compliant tenancy or hide the child-compartment targets entirely. Cloned detector recipes are the third trap, since a target can carry a recipe whose individual rules have been switched off or had their risk levels lowered; inspect the effective rules, not just the recipe's presence. Cloud Guard has a single reporting region, so problems are visible only there, and the set of monitored regions must be confirmed separately.

controls.title: Cloud Guard detections reach a person, not only the console
controls.objective: Cloud Guard findings nobody sees are not a control. Detected problems should be pushed to an alerting channel as they are raised rather than waiting for someone to open the console.
controls.procedure: Determine the reporting region from `oci cloud-guard configuration get --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid>`. In that region, list Events rules for the tenancy root and every ACTIVE compartment (`oci events rule list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <reporting-region>`) and read each with `oci events rule get --rule-id <ocid>`, matching `condition` on `com.oraclecloud.cloudguard.problemdetected`. Read the entire condition, not only the eventType array, so additionalDetails filters are visible. Record the rule's `compartment-id`, verify `is-enabled: true` on the rule and `is-enabled: true` on the ONS action, then resolve the topic with `oci ons topic get --topic-id <ocid>` and `oci ons subscription list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <reporting-region>`.
controls.evidence: An Events rule in the reporting region whose `compartment-id` is the tenancy OCID, whose `condition` contains com.oraclecloud.cloudguard.problemdetected together with any additionalDetails filters present verbatim, `is-enabled: true`, and an ONS action (`is-enabled: true`) whose topic has a subscription in lifecycle-state ACTIVE.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when an enabled Events rule whose `compartment-id` equals the tenancy OCID exists in the Cloud Guard reporting region, matches com.oraclecloud.cloudguard.problemdetected, and publishes through an enabled ONS action to a topic with >=1 ACTIVE subscription. A rule in another region, a rule in a child compartment, a disabled ONS action, or a condition narrowed by additionalDetails so that lower-risk problems are dropped without documented acceptance, FAILs.
controls.remediation: `oci events rule create --region <reporting-region> --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --display-name cloudguard-problems --is-enabled true --condition '{"eventType":["com.oraclecloud.cloudguard.problemdetected"]}' --actions '{"actions":[{"actionType":"ONS","isEnabled":true,"topicId":"<ocid>"}]}'`. Optionally add a Cloud Guard responder or a second rule dedicated to high-risk problems, but keep an unfiltered rule as the baseline.
controls.caveat: Cloud Guard emits problem events only in the reporting region, so a rule built in the home region when the reporting region differs never fires while looking entirely correct. Scoping the rule to a child compartment limits it to that subtree, so capture and test the rule's `compartment-id`. Narrowing the condition with additionalDetails filters (for example only CRITICAL risk) reduces coverage in a way a presence check will not notice, so read the whole condition rather than just the eventType array, and check the ONS action's own enabled flag. The control is also meaningless while 4.14 fails, because no targets means no problems to notify on.

controls.title: Re-key customer-managed vault keys on a cycle no longer than one year
controls.objective: Rotating a master encryption key limits how much data a single compromised key version can decrypt and bounds the blast radius of key material exposure.
controls.procedure: Build the compartment set once: `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all`. Per region from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`, list vaults across every compartment with `oci kms vault list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>`. For each vault in lifecycle-state ACTIVE take its `management-endpoint`, then iterate the FULL compartment set against that one endpoint — a key's compartment is independent of its vault's compartment — running `oci kms management key list --compartment-id <c> --endpoint <mgmt-endpoint> --all` for every compartment c. For every key with lifecycle-state ENABLED run `oci kms management key-version list --key-id <ocid> --endpoint <mgmt-endpoint> --all` and compute the newest `time-created`. Compare that timestamp with the assessment date and record `protection-mode`.
api: oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all
oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query vault resources where lifecycleState = 'ACTIVE'" --region <region> --all
controls.evidence: Per key OCID: the (vault OCID, key compartment OCID) pair, the maximum `time-created` across its key-version list, the key's `protection-mode` and `lifecycle-state`, and the owning vault's region and management endpoint. Record the number of compartments queried per vault so an under-scoped enumeration is visible.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when, for every ENABLED customer-managed key found by iterating every compartment against every ACTIVE vault's management endpoint in every subscribed region, the newest key version's `time-created` is within 365 days of the assessment date. A vault in lifecycle-state ACTIVE that yields zero keys across all compartments is an enumeration error and must be reported as such, never scored as a pass. Keys with `protection-mode: EXTERNAL` are recorded as documented exceptions rather than automatic FAILs.
controls.remediation: Rotate each stale key with `oci kms management key-version create --key-id <ocid> --endpoint <vault-management-endpoint>`. Then enable Vault auto-rotation where the key type and protection mode support it, or add a scheduled job, and re-encrypt or re-wrap data that must move to the new version for services that do not do so transparently (for example `oci os bucket reencrypt` for Object Storage).
controls.caveat: Two enumeration traps precede any evaluation. First, the management commands fail without `--endpoint <vault management-endpoint>` because the KMS management API is per-vault rather than regional, and an assessor who omits it sees an error and may record a vacuous pass. Second, listing keys only in the vault's own compartment misses every key created in a workload compartment inside a centrally owned vault, which is the normal enterprise layout — iterate the full compartment set against each vault endpoint and treat a zero-key ACTIVE vault as a broken enumeration. Only customer-created keys are in scope; Oracle-managed keys must not be flagged. Keys with `protection-mode: EXTERNAL` live in a third-party HSM and cannot be rotated through this API, so they need a documented exception. Creating a new key version does not re-encrypt existing data, so a fresh rotation date does not prove old ciphertext left the old version.

controls.title: Record object write operations for every Object Storage bucket
controls.objective: Write-level Object Storage logs are the only record of who created, overwrote or deleted an object. Without them, data tampering and staged exfiltration inside a bucket cannot be reconstructed.
controls.procedure: Get the tenancy-global namespace with `oci os ns get` (no region argument — the namespace is not regional). Build the compartment set with `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all`. For each subscribed region from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`, enumerate buckets with `oci os bucket list -ns <namespace> --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>` per compartment, or `oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query bucket resources" --region <r> --all`. Then enumerate logs across the whole compartment set: `oci logging log-group list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>` and `oci logging log list --log-group-id <ocid> --all --region <r>`. Match logs where `configuration.source.service` is objectstorage, `configuration.source.category` is write, and `configuration.source.resource` equals the bucket NAME, requiring the log's region to equal the bucket's region.
api: oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all
oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query bucket resources" --region <region> --all
controls.evidence: For each bucket name plus its compartment and region: a log with `lifecycle-state: ACTIVE`, `is-enabled: true`, `configuration.source.service: objectstorage`, `configuration.source.category: write`, `configuration.source.resource` equal to that bucket's name, and the log's own region matching the bucket's. Record bucket counts per region so a silent enumeration failure is visible.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when every bucket in every subscribed region is matched by a Logging log that is both `lifecycle-state: ACTIVE` and `is-enabled: true`, of service objectstorage and category write, whose `source.resource` equals the bucket name AND whose region equals the bucket's region. Any unmatched bucket is a FAIL; a name match across different regions does not count.
controls.remediation: `oci logging log create --log-group-id <ocid> --display-name <bucket>-write --log-type SERVICE --is-enabled true --retention-duration 90 --region <r> --configuration '{"compartmentId":"<ocid>","source":{"sourceType":"OCISERVICE","service":"objectstorage","resource":"<bucket-name>","category":"write"}}'`, repeated for every bucket in every region, and wired into the bucket-provisioning pipeline so new buckets never ship without it.
controls.caveat: Object Storage log sources are keyed by bucket NAME, not OCID, and bucket names are unique only within a namespace-and-region pair, so matching names without also matching the log's region can pair a bucket in one region with a log in another and produce a false pass. Buckets are namespace-scoped but compartment-assigned and can be moved between compartments, so a root-compartment-only enumeration under-counts, and a compartment walk run with `--access-level ACCESSIBLE` can silently drop compartments along with their buckets. A `read` category log does not satisfy this control, and a log that exists with `is-enabled: false` or in CREATING/FAILED state records nothing. New buckets are the usual gap: this is a point-in-time snapshot unless logging is enforced at provisioning.

controls.title: Alert on interactive console sign-in by local (non-federated) users
controls.objective: Local IAM users bypass the enterprise IdP and its conditional-access controls, so every interactive console sign-in by such an account should raise a notification and unexpected break-glass use gets caught.
controls.procedure: Work in the tenancy home region. List Events rules for the tenancy root and each ACTIVE compartment with `oci events rule list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <home>` and read each with `oci events rule get --rule-id <ocid>`; match `condition` on `com.oraclecloud.identitysignon.interactivelogin`. Record the rule's `compartment-id`, confirm `is-enabled: true` on the rule and `is-enabled: true` on the ONS action, then resolve the topic via `oci ons topic get --topic-id <ocid>` and confirm a subscription with lifecycle-state ACTIVE. Cross-reference the local account population across every identity domain, not just legacy IAM: enumerate domains with `oci iam domain list --compartment-id <ocid> --all` (repeat over the compartment tree), read each domain's `url`, and list users with the plural form `oci identity-domains users list --endpoint <domain-url> --all`; supplement with `oci iam user list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --all` for the legacy/default-domain population.
controls.evidence: The rule OCID and its `compartment-id`, the `condition` containing com.oraclecloud.identitysignon.interactivelogin, `is-enabled: true`, and an ONS action (`is-enabled: true`) whose topic-id resolves to an ACTIVE topic with a subscription in lifecycle-state ACTIVE; plus the per-domain local-user inventory used to justify the alert's relevance.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when an Events rule whose `compartment-id` equals the tenancy OCID (root compartment) exists in the tenancy home region with `is-enabled: true`, matches com.oraclecloud.identitysignon.interactivelogin, and delivers through an ONS action with `is-enabled: true` to a topic with >=1 ACTIVE subscription. Sign-on events surface at the root, so a rule anchored in a child compartment FAILs.
controls.remediation: `oci events rule create --region <home> --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --display-name local-user-signin --is-enabled true --condition '{"eventType":["com.oraclecloud.identitysignon.interactivelogin"]}' --actions '{"actions":[{"actionType":"ONS","isEnabled":true,"topicId":"<ocid>"}]}'`. Pair it with reducing the local-user population, in every domain, to documented break-glass accounts only, and enable the domain's own sign-on notification where the tenancy uses identity domains.
controls.caveat: Sign-on events are emitted only in the home region and surface at the root compartment, so a rule elsewhere — by region or by compartment — is inert while looking correct. The event covers interactive console logins by local users; federated logins are authenticated at the IdP and never appear here, so this must not be read as full authentication monitoring. In identity-domain tenancies sign-on telemetry is produced by the domain and the legacy identitysignon event type may not fire, which makes a syntactically correct rule a false pass; the population itself is also under-counted by `oci iam user list`, which returns only the legacy/default-domain users, so enumerate every domain with `oci iam domain list` plus the plural `oci identity-domains users list`. Whether an alert is actually triaged by a human is a process question the API cannot settle.

controls.title: Deny anonymous internet read on every Object Storage bucket
controls.objective: No bucket should serve objects to unauthenticated callers. An OCI bucket set to ObjectRead or ObjectReadWithoutList is reachable over the public Object Storage endpoint with no signed request, so any object in it is world-readable and the only remaining protection is the obscurity of the object name.
controls.procedure: Get the tenancy-global namespace with `oci os ns get`. Enumerate subscribed regions with `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>` and every ACTIVE compartment including the tenancy root with `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all` (`--include-root` is valueless; `--access-level ACCESSIBLE` can silently drop compartments for an auditor principal and hide their buckets). Buckets are regional, so per region run resource search for Bucket to collect names and compartments, then call `oci os bucket get -ns <ns> --name <bucket> --region <r>` on each, because list output and resource search both omit `public-access-type`. Read `public-access-type`. Also list pre-authenticated requests per bucket, since a PAR grants unauthenticated access independently of that field.
api: oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all
oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query bucket resources" --region <region> --all
controls.evidence: The `public-access-type` field of each `oci os bucket get` response, keyed by namespace + bucket name + compartment OCID + region; plus the full `oci os preauth-request list` array for each bucket with each PAR's `access-type`, `object-name` and `time-expires`; plus the compartment and region counts enumerated.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when, for every bucket in every subscribed region and every compartment, `public-access-type` == "NoPublicAccess" AND the bucket carries no pre-authenticated request whose `time-expires` is in the future and whose `access-type` confers read (ObjectRead, ObjectReadWrite, AnyObjectRead or AnyObjectReadWrite). Any other `public-access-type` value FAILs, as does any live read-capable PAR. A run that inspected fewer regions or compartments than were enumerated is inconclusive, not a pass.
controls.remediation: Set the bucket back to private: `oci os bucket update -ns <namespace> --name <bucket> --public-access-type NoPublicAccess`. Delete unnecessary PARs with `oci os preauth-request delete -ns <namespace> --bucket-name <bucket> --par-id <id>`. Prevent recurrence with an IAM policy denying `object-family` public-access changes and enable the Cloud Guard public-bucket detector rule for continuous detection.
controls.caveat: Four false-pass traps. (1) The Object Storage namespace is tenancy-wide but buckets are per-region: a check that only queries the home region silently passes buckets in every other subscribed region, and `oci iam region-subscription list --all` is not a valid invocation (the operation is not paginated) — use `--tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`, or the region loop dies on its first call and the whole sweep never runs. (2) `oci os bucket list` does not return publicAccessType, and neither does resource search, so an assessor who stops at the list sees no evidence of exposure and reports clean — a per-bucket `bucket get` is mandatory. (3) A bucket with NoPublicAccess is still anonymously readable through an unexpired pre-authenticated request; PARs are invisible to the bucket's own access-type field and are the most common way an audited-clean bucket is actually public. (4) Enumerating compartments with `--access-level ACCESSIBLE` drops compartments the auditor cannot directly inspect, and their buckets are then never examined at all. Cloud Guard problem state is a detective signal only and lags configuration, so it must not be used as the primary verdict; confirm the detector rule id for the tenancy with `detector-recipe-detector-rule list` rather than hard-coding a guessed constant, and note the `get` operation is keyed only on recipe id plus rule id.

controls.title: Back Object Storage buckets with a tenancy-owned Vault key
controls.objective: Buckets encrypted with the Oracle-managed default key give the tenancy no ability to rotate, disable, or destroy the encryption material. Binding each bucket to a Vault (KMS) master encryption key the customer owns puts crypto-shredding and rotation under tenancy control and makes key use auditable.
controls.procedure: Resolve the namespace via `oci os ns get` and the regions via `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`. Build the compartment set with `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all`. For each subscribed region, enumerate buckets across all compartments (tenancy root included) using resource search for Bucket, then call `oci os bucket get -ns <ns> --name <bucket> --region <r>` per bucket and read `kms-key-id`. A null or absent value means the Oracle-managed key. For every non-null key OCID, verify the key itself with `oci kms management key get --key-id <ocid> --endpoint <vault-management-endpoint>` against that key's own vault management endpoint and confirm `lifecycle-state: ENABLED`, not PENDING_DELETION or DISABLED.

oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query bucket resources" --region <region> --all

controls.verdict_rule: PASS when every bucket in every subscribed region and compartment returns a non-null `kms-key-id` whose referenced Vault key resolves and is in `lifecycle-state: ENABLED`. Null, empty, or a key OCID that is DISABLED / PENDING_DELETION / unresolvable FAILs. A region or compartment that was not enumerated cannot be scored as a pass.

Re-encrypt pre-existing objects with `oci os bucket reencrypt -ns <ns> --bucket-name <bucket>`.
controls.caveat: Setting `kms-key-id` on an existing bucket only governs newly written objects — objects already stored keep their previous data-encryption-key wrapping until an explicit re-encrypt completes, so a bucket can show a customer key while its historical objects are still under the Oracle-managed key. A key OCID that merely exists is not sufficient evidence either: the vault or key may be disabled or scheduled for deletion, in which case the field passes a string match but the control's intent (usable customer-controlled rotation) is not met. Buckets are regional — a home-region-only sweep produces a false pass, and `oci iam region-subscription list --all` is invalid, so drive the loop with `--tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`. The key OCID may live in a different compartment or region than the bucket; resolve it against its own vault management endpoint rather than assuming locality. Cloud Guard here is corroboration only and never the verdict source: its `detector-recipe-detector-rule get` takes recipe id plus rule id (no `--detector-id`), and the applicable rule id — the Oracle-managed-key bucket rule, e.g. BUCKET_IS_ENCRYPTED_WITH_ORACLE_MANAGED_KEY — must be read from `detector-recipe-detector-rule list` for the tenancy rather than assumed.

controls.title: Keep prior object generations recoverable on all buckets
controls.objective: With versioning off, an overwrite or delete of an object is unrecoverable, so a single compromised credential or a scripted mistake permanently destroys data. Enabling versioning makes Object Storage retain superseded and deleted object generations, which is the tenancy's only native rollback for ransomware or accidental deletion.
controls.procedure: Resolve the namespace with `oci os ns get`. Build the full compartment set from the tenancy root with `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all` (the flag takes no value, and ACCESSIBLE would truncate the tree), and the region set from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`. For each region, list buckets per compartment with `oci os bucket list -ns <namespace> --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>`, then call `oci os bucket get -ns <ns> --name <bucket> --region <r>` on each bucket and read the `versioning` field, whose values are Enabled, Suspended, or Disabled. Read the bucket's object-lifecycle policy as well, since a rule deleting previous versions defeats the control. Record the value per bucket, not per compartment.
api: oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all
controls.evidence: The `versioning` field of each `oci os bucket get` response, recorded against namespace, bucket name, compartment OCID and region, together with the bucket's `oci os object-lifecycle-policy get` rules (target, action, time-amount) and the compartment/region counts enumerated.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when every bucket in every subscribed region and compartment returns `versioning` == "Enabled" AND no object-lifecycle rule on that bucket deletes previous object versions inside the organisation's recovery window. A value of "Suspended" or "Disabled" FAILs; a bucket that could not be inspected counts as FAIL, not as absent.
controls.remediation: Enable retention of prior generations with `oci os bucket update -ns <ns> --name <bucket> --versioning Enabled`. For buckets already carrying versions, review object-lifecycle rules (`oci os object-lifecycle-policy get -ns <ns> --bucket-name <bucket>`) so that a DELETE action on previous versions does not defeat the control, and pair versioning with a retention rule where immutability is required.
controls.caveat: "Suspended" is the principal false pass: a bucket that once had versioning enabled and was later suspended still shows a non-Disabled value and retains old versions, but new overwrites are no longer protected — a naive truthiness check on the field passes it. Second trap: versioning is a per-bucket setting with no compartment or tenancy inheritance, so sampling one bucket says nothing about its siblings, and a walk that omits the tenancy root compartment misses buckets created there — `oci iam compartment list` does not return the root unless the valueless `--include-root` flag is passed (or the root OCID is appended manually), and `--access-level ACCESSIBLE` can drop further compartments silently. Third: versioning does not survive a lifecycle policy that deletes previous versions after N days, so the object-lifecycle-policy read is needed for a truthful verdict. Fourth: the region loop must be driven by `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`; the `--all` form is rejected and takes the whole multi-region sweep down with it.

controls.title: Attach a customer Vault key to every block volume
controls.objective: Block volumes are always encrypted at rest, but by default with an Oracle-managed key that the tenancy cannot rotate, disable, or destroy. Assigning a Vault master encryption key owned by the tenancy makes the volume's encryption material subject to customer rotation policy and enables crypto-shredding of a decommissioned volume.
controls.procedure: Block volumes are regional and compartment-scoped. For each region from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`, use resource search for volume resources to collect every volume OCID tenancy-wide in one call — `oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query volume resources where lifecycleState = 'AVAILABLE'" --region <r> --all` (the searchable attribute is `lifecycleState`; the mis-cased form matches nothing and returns an empty, clean-looking result). Otherwise enumerate compartments with `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all` and call `oci bv volume list --compartment-id <ocid> --all --region <r>` per compartment. Then `oci bv volume get --volume-id <ocid> --region <r>` on each and read `kms-key-id`. Restrict scoring to lifecycle-state AVAILABLE volumes, verify each referenced key is ENABLED via its vault management endpoint, and assert a non-zero volume count wherever compute instances exist so a silently empty query cannot be scored as a pass.
api: oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query volume resources where lifecycleState = 'AVAILABLE'" --region <region> --all
oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all
controls.evidence: The `kms-key-id` field of each `oci bv volume get` response, keyed by volume OCID, compartment OCID and region, with the matching `lifecycle-state` (and `protection-mode`) of the key from `oci kms management key get`; plus the per-region volume counts and the corresponding compute-instance counts used as the non-zero sanity check.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when every block volume in lifecycle-state AVAILABLE, in every subscribed region and every compartment, has a non-null `kms-key-id` resolving to a Vault key in lifecycle-state ENABLED. Null or absent `kms-key-id`, or a key that is DISABLED/PENDING_DELETION/unresolvable, FAILs. A region whose enumeration returned zero volumes while compute instances exist there is an enumeration error, not a pass. Volumes in PROVISIONING or TERMINATED state are excluded from scoring.
controls.remediation: A volume's key is assigned through the dedicated KMS-key operation, not through volume update: `oci bv volume-kms-key update --volume-id <ocid> --kms-key-id <key-ocid>` (read the current assignment with `oci bv volume-kms-key get --volume-id <ocid>`, and revert to the Oracle-managed key with `oci bv volume-kms-key delete --volume-id <ocid>`). Grant the Block Volume service key usage first, e.g. `Allow service blockstorage to use keys in compartment <c>`. For volumes that cannot be updated, create a CMK-encrypted clone or restore from a CMK-encrypted backup and swap the attachment. Re-key backups and cross-region replicas as well.
controls.caveat: The key assignment is not inherited from anywhere — not from the compartment, not from the source image, not from the instance — so it must be read on each volume individually. Three traps produce false passes: (1) a single-region check, since volumes exist independently in each subscribed region and resource search only answers for the region of the endpoint it is called against (and `region-subscription list --all` is an invalid invocation that kills the loop outright); (2) a structured-search query using the non-existent `lifeCycleState` attribute, which returns nothing and reads as a tenancy with no volumes — always assert a non-zero count where instances exist; (3) treating a non-null key OCID as sufficient when the key or its vault is DISABLED or PENDING_DELETION, which leaves the field populated but the control unmet. Also note that volume backups and cross-region replicas carry their own `kms-key-id` and are commonly left on the Oracle-managed key even when the source volume is compliant, so a volume-only sweep overstates coverage. Volumes in PROVISIONING or TERMINATED state should be excluded from scoring rather than counted as passes.

controls.title: Boot volumes must reference a tenancy-owned Vault key
controls.objective: The boot volume holds the operating system, its configuration and often credentials cached by the instance. Left on the Oracle-managed default key, that data cannot be crypto-shredded or re-keyed by the tenancy; binding it to a customer Vault key brings the instance's root disk under the same key lifecycle as other regulated data.
controls.procedure: For each region from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`, collect boot volume OCIDs tenancy-wide with `oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query bootvolume resources where lifecycleState = 'AVAILABLE'" --region <r> --all` — materially better than the CLI list, because `oci bv boot-volume list` requires both `--compartment-id` and `--availability-domain`, forcing an AD x compartment cross-product. Note the attribute spelling: `lifecycleState`, not `lifeCycleState`, which matches nothing and yields the zero-boot-volumes result this control is written to prevent. Then call `oci bv boot-volume get --boot-volume-id <ocid> --region <r>` per OCID and read `kms-key-id`. Score only AVAILABLE boot volumes, confirm each referenced Vault key is ENABLED, and assert the boot-volume count is non-zero wherever compute instances exist.
api: oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query bootvolume resources where lifecycleState = 'AVAILABLE'" --region <region> --all
oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all
controls.evidence: The `kms-key-id` field of each `oci bv boot-volume get` response, recorded with the boot volume OCID, its availability domain, compartment OCID and region, plus the key's `lifecycle-state` from `oci kms management key get`; and the per-region boot-volume and instance counts supporting the non-zero assertion.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when every boot volume in lifecycle-state AVAILABLE, across all subscribed regions, all compartments and all availability domains, returns a non-null `kms-key-id` that resolves to an ENABLED Vault key. Null or unresolvable FAILs. A region reporting zero boot volumes while compute instances exist there is an enumeration failure and must not be scored as a pass.
controls.remediation: Re-key through the dedicated KMS-key operation — the boot-volume update operation does not accept a key assignment: `oci bv boot-volume-kms-key update --boot-volume-id <ocid> --kms-key-id <key-ocid>` (with `oci bv boot-volume-kms-key get/delete` to read and remove). Grant `Allow service blockstorage to use keys in compartment <c>` first. For instances that must be rebuilt, launch them with `--source-details` carrying the kmsKeyId so the boot volume is created against the customer key from the start. Re-key boot volume backups too.
controls.caveat: The dominant trap is enumeration rather than evaluation: `oci bv boot-volume list` mandates an availability domain, so a script that iterates compartments but not ADs quietly returns nothing for multi-AD regions and reports a clean tenancy with zero boot volumes examined — and the resource-search alternative fails the same way if the query uses `lifeCycleState` instead of `lifecycleState`. Prefer resource search, spell the attribute correctly, and assert that the count of boot volumes found is non-zero wherever compute instances exist. Three further traps: `oci iam region list` returns all OCI regions rather than the ones this tenancy is subscribed to, and `oci iam region-subscription list --all` is rejected outright, so `region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>` must drive the loop; a boot volume detached from a stopped or terminated instance still exists and still holds OS data, so filtering to attached volumes understates exposure; and boot volume backups hold their own key reference and are frequently non-compliant even when the live volume is.

controls.title: File Storage file systems must use a customer-controlled Vault key
controls.objective: OCI File Storage encrypts every file system at rest, but the default Oracle-managed key leaves key rotation, disablement and destruction outside the tenancy's control. Pointing each file system at a Vault master encryption key the customer owns lets the organisation rotate on its own schedule and render a decommissioned NFS export unreadable by destroying the key.
controls.procedure: File systems are regional and availability-domain scoped. For each region from `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`, use `oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query filesystem resources where lifecycleState = 'ACTIVE'" --region <r> --all` to obtain every file system OCID tenancy-wide in one call (the attribute is `lifecycleState`; the mis-cased form returns nothing and, because this query is the primary enumeration, means no file systems are examined at all). The CLI alternative, `oci fs file-system list`, requires both `--compartment-id` and `--availability-domain`, so it needs a compartment x AD cross-product driven by `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all` and `oci iam availability-domain list`. Before accepting an empty result, corroborate against `oci fs mount-target list --compartment-id <ocid> --availability-domain <ad> --all --region <r>`. Call `oci fs file-system get --file-system-id <ocid> --region <r>` per OCID, read `kms-key-id`, and verify each referenced key resolves to an ENABLED Vault key.
api: oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query filesystem resources where lifecycleState = 'ACTIVE'" --region <region> --all
oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --include-root --all
controls.evidence: The `kms-key-id` field of each `oci fs file-system get` response, recorded with file system OCID, availability domain, compartment OCID and region, alongside the key's `lifecycle-state` from `oci kms management key get`, and the per-region/per-AD file-system and mount-target counts used to validate the enumeration.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS when every file system in lifecycle-state ACTIVE, across all subscribed regions, compartments and availability domains, returns a non-null `kms-key-id` that resolves to a Vault key in lifecycle-state ENABLED. Null, empty or unresolvable FAILs. An empty file-system enumeration in a region that has mount targets is an enumeration error and must be reported as inconclusive rather than as a pass.
controls.remediation: Assign the key in place with `oci fs file-system update --file-system-id <ocid> --kms-key-id <key-ocid>`, having first granted the service access, e.g. `Allow service FssOc1Prod to use key-delegate in compartment <c>` (the service principal name is realm-specific). Where a file system cannot be updated, create a CMK-backed file system and migrate the data, then delete the original so the old key material is retired. Re-create clones and snapshots taken under the previous key.
controls.caveat: `oci fs file-system list` will not run without an availability domain, so the classic false pass is an assessor looping compartments only, getting empty result sets and concluding there are no file systems in the tenancy. Drive the enumeration from resource search — with `lifecycleState` spelled correctly, since a malformed query fails the same way silently — and corroborate a zero result against the mount targets that exist per AD. Also note `oci iam region-subscription list --all` is an invalid invocation; use `--tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>` or the region loop never starts. Two more: the service policy granting FSS use of the key is region- and realm-specific (the service principal name differs between realms), so a file system can carry a key OCID that the service can no longer use, which the `kms-key-id` field alone will not reveal — resolving the key and confirming ENABLED is the minimum corroboration. Finally, `kms-key-id` describes the file system, not the exports or snapshots taken before the key was assigned; clones and snapshots created under the previous key are not re-keyed by this update.

controls.title: Verify the tenancy is subdivided into operator-defined compartments
controls.objective: The tenancy root should not be the only container: workloads belong in dedicated compartments so IAM policies, quotas, budgets and audit scoping can be applied per boundary instead of tenancy-wide.
controls.procedure: Resolve the tenancy OCID (CLI config `tenancy=`, or `oci iam compartment get --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid>`). Compartments are global IAM objects, so one call against the home region suffices: `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --all`. The subtree flag returns the whole nested tree, so no recursion and no region loop are needed; `--include-root` is deliberately omitted here because the root itself must not count toward segmentation (and note the flag takes no value if you add it for another purpose). Count entries with `lifecycle-state` ACTIVE, excluding Oracle's `ManagedCompartmentForPaaS`.
api: oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --all
oci iam compartment list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ANY --lifecycle-state ACTIVE --all
oci search resource structured-search --query-text "query compartment resources where lifecycleState = 'ACTIVE'" --region <home-region> --all
controls.evidence: `data[]` from `oci iam compartment list --compartment-id-in-subtree true`: each entry's `id` (ocid1.compartment...), `name`, and `lifecycle-state`, plus the tenancy OCID used as the root argument and the total entry count returned.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS if the subtree listing contains at least one compartment whose `lifecycle-state` == ACTIVE and whose `name` != 'ManagedCompartmentForPaaS'. Otherwise FAIL. Compartments in CREATING, DELETING or DELETED state never count, and a listing produced with `--access-level ACCESSIBLE` or under a principal lacking tenancy-wide inspect is inconclusive rather than a pass.
controls.remediation: Create a compartment structure mirroring ownership/environment boundaries: `oci iam compartment create --compartment-id <parent-ocid> --name <name> --description <text>`. Nest sub-compartments for per-environment isolation, move existing resources out of the tenancy root with each service's change-compartment call, then write IAM policies scoped to the new compartment OCIDs.
controls.caveat: Three false passes: (1) counting `ManagedCompartmentForPaaS`, which Oracle creates automatically for PaaS services and proves no deliberate segmentation; (2) counting compartments in CREATING/DELETING/DELETED state — always filter on `lifecycle-state`, or pass `--lifecycle-state ACTIVE`; (3) an existing-but-empty compartment satisfies the letter of the check while every real resource still sits at the tenancy level, so this control is only meaningful when evaluated together with 6.2. Operationally, running as a principal without tenancy-wide inspect rights, or passing `--access-level ACCESSIBLE` instead of `ANY`, silently truncates the tree and can turn a populated tenancy into an apparent zero-compartment result — record the returned count as evidence so truncation is visible. Resource Search is an accelerator only: confirm `compartment` is an indexed type with `oci search resource-type list` before relying on it, and treat `oci iam compartment list` as the authoritative enumeration.

controls.title: Confirm no workload resources are deployed directly at the tenancy level
controls.objective: Anything created straight under the tenancy inherits the broadest possible policy scope and cannot be isolated, quota-limited or delegated; workload resources therefore belong in child compartments, leaving the tenancy level for identity constructs only.
controls.procedure: Get the tenancy OCID and every subscribed region: `oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id <tenancy-ocid>`. Search is a regional endpoint, so loop regions: `oci search resource structured-search --region <r> --query-text "query all resources where compartmentId = '<tenancy-ocid>'" --all`, letting the CLI page rather than hand-rolling `opc-next-page` handling, so a partial first page can never be scored as an empty tenancy root. Confirm which types Search actually indexes with `oci search resource-type list`, then cross-check the unindexed services per region with direct list calls scoped to the tenancy OCID: `oci compute instance list --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --region <r> --all`, `oci network vcn list`, `oci bv volume list`, and `oci os bucket list -ns <namespace> --compartment-id <tenancy-ocid> --region <r> --all` (the namespace comes from `oci os ns get`, which is tenancy-global and takes no region).
api: oci search resource structured-search --region <region> --query-text "query all resources where compartmentId = '<tenancy-ocid>'" --all

oci search resource structured-search --region <region> --query-text "query instance, vcn, volume, bootvolume, bucket, filesystem, autonomousdatabase, dbsystem, loadbalancer resources where compartmentId = '<tenancy-ocid>' && lifecycleState != 'TERMINATED'" --all
controls.evidence: Per region, the `data.items[]` array from `oci search resource structured-search`: each item's `identifier`, `resource-type`, `display-name`, `lifecycle-state` and `compartment-id` equal to the tenancy OCID; plus the per-service list results for the unindexed types, the region list used, and the resource-type list Search reported as indexed.
controls.verdict_rule: PASS if, for every subscribed region, the tenancy-OCID-scoped search plus the per-service cross-checks return zero items after excluding TERMINATED/DELETED states and tenancy-only types (compartments, users, groups, policies, dynamic groups, identity domains, tag namespaces and tag defaults, budgets, `ManagedCompartmentForPaaS`). A region that was not queried, or a search truncated by unhandled pagination, makes the result inconclusive rather than a pass.
controls.remediation: Move each item into a purpose-built compartment with that service's change-compartment call, e.g. `oci compute instance change-compartment --instance-id <ocid> --compartment-id <target>` or, for a bucket, `oci os bucket update -ns <namespace> --name <bucket> --compartment-id <target-compartment-ocid>`. Prevent recurrence by narrowing `manage` policies to child compartments and setting a zero quota at the tenancy level.
controls.caveat: Two structural false passes. First, querying only the home region — Search is a per-region service, so a stray instance, volume or bucket in another subscribed region is invisible unless every entry from `region-subscription list` is iterated. Second, trusting Search alone: it indexes only resource types registered with it (verify with `oci search resource-type list`), so newly released or unsupported services never appear and must be enumerated with per-service list calls against the tenancy OCID; and a hand-rolled pagination loop that stops after the first page produces the same empty-looking result, so let the CLI page with `--all`. Conversely, expect legitimate tenancy-level residents that must NOT be flagged: IAM users, groups, policies, dynamic groups and compartments themselves, identity domains, tag namespaces and tag defaults, budgets, `ManagedCompartmentForPaaS`, and Oracle-managed objects; in an identity-domains tenancy the users and groups live inside the domain rather than legacy IAM but the domain itself is still a tenancy-level object. Object Storage buckets have namespace-unique names yet a real per-bucket compartment assignment, so they must be listed per region against the tenancy OCID (`-ns`/`--namespace-name` selects the namespace, `--name` selects a bucket on get/update) rather than assumed global — and the namespace itself is tenancy-global, so `oci os ns get` takes no region. Finally, filter out TERMINATED/DELETED items or long-dead resources will produce false FAILs.
